Executive Order 10044 (official Federal Register text, 14 FR 1227, PDF pages 1-1, read in the saved OCR text layer of the govinfo issue PDF: heading, enacting clause, operative text and signature/filing line are all present) permits Atomic Energy Commission employees, with the General Manager's approval, to hold office as constables, deputy sheriffs or other law enforcement officers and other state or local offices, subject to a non-interference determination. Its whole operative content is an amendment of Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873, as amended (the 1989 OFR disposition table: 'Amended EO 9'; 'Revoked by EO 11408'). EO 11408 of April 25, 1968 (33 FR 6459, saved official text read in full) revoked EO 9 itself in section 1 and in section 2 revoked 'All prior Executive orders insofar as they interpret or amend Executive Order No. 9'; EO 11408 section 2 names it expressly in its list of revoked amendatory orders. Because the order consists only of that amendment, 'insofar as' reaches all of it, which is also why the OFR catalog's '(in part)' qualifier on some of these notes does not leave any part in force. EO 11408 states no effective date, so the revocation took effect on signing, 1968-04-25. No earlier end was found: the order has no expiry, condition or temporary term, the OFR catalog and the saved-text corpus show no earlier amendment or revocation, and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches show no current citation. Each clause therefore first ended on 1968-04-25 and that is the whole-order end. OCR quotations keep the scan's recognition errors (and soft hyphens) exactly as held; they have not been compared with page images.

EO 11408 contains no savings, transition or continuation clause. Its section 1 revoked Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873 (the dual federal-state office-holding prohibition) itself, and section 2 revoked every prior order insofar as it interpreted or amended that order. This order's only operative content is an amendment of (an exception to) that 1873 order, so once the prohibition itself was revoked nothing remained for the exception to operate on, and no office, fund, property, entitlement or enforceable right was created by the order that could survive; office-holding done under the permission before 1968 was lawful when done and is a completed historical fact, not a continuing effect.

express revocation by EO 12553 (51 FR 7237): 'the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked', table row '10054 Modifying provisions for transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations'; EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the effective date is the on_signing reading, February 25, 1986 (signed THE WHITE HOUSE, February 25, 1986; Federal Register publication 1986-03-03 is not an effective date)

EO 10054 (signed 1949-04-29, 14 FR 2129, read in full from the held official FR text, sha256 of the downloaded page file 02f3bed2...), one paragraph, modifies para. 3(a) of EO 9721 for one named person: the three-year limit is replaced by five years from the beginning of Gross's service with the International Telecommunication Union. EO 12553 (reading record LSP-EO_12553, read once in full; the table row '10054 Modifying provisions for transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations') revokes the order outright, with no effective-date wording; the claim therefore rests on the on_signing reading, 1986-02-25, and treats that date as an upper bound, not a certified end. Inventory: the dossier's single clause (chars 826-2170) covers the whole operative paragraph from 'By virtue of the authority' to the end of the proviso and the order has no other section; kept. Earlier-end tests. (1) Own terms: the order has no sunset or termination clause. The five-year period is a condition on when Gross's service must end to carry the reemployment right; it does not say the modification expires, and its start date (the unheld beginning of his service) is not needed to find an end because it is not an end. A window or report-type deadline is never an end. (2) Parent chain: Parent-order chain read in the held official texts: EO 9721 (11 FR 5209, May 10, 1946) para. 3(a) reemploys an employee whose international-organization service is 'terminated without prejudice within three years from the date of such transfer' and requires application within ninety days after termination; EO 9949 (13 FR 2089, 1948-04-17) gave the same five-year relief to Paul D. Miles; EO 10103 (1950-02-01) amends only secs. 1 and 2 of EO 9721 and does not touch para. 3(a) or name EO 10054; EO 10804 (24 FR 1147, signed 1959-02-12) sec. 2 revokes EO 9721, EO 10103 and EO 10774 'except that each shall be considered to remain in effect' for employees serving with an international organization on the enactment date of the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act (72 Stat. 961) who do not elect its coverage 'and for the purposes of any rights and benefits vested under each such order' before that date; EO 11138 (1964-01-07, Frederick Strauss) and EO 11303 (1966-09-12, Reginald C. Price) waive limits in EO 9721 for other named persons. EO 10804 names neither EO 10054, EO 9949 nor EO 10415, revokes only the parent, and expressly keeps rights vested under it; because Gross's window had closed by 1954-04-29 at the latest, nothing but already vested rights could remain under the modification in 1959, so the 1959 partial revocation of the parent neither ends nor changes this clause and is ruled out as an earlier end (it is not attachable as a structured later event because the dossier holds no ACT record for it; the held official text was read). EO 11138 and EO 11303 name other persons and EO 10103 does not touch para. 3(a), so all three are ruled out. EO 12553's table lists EO 9721, 9949, 10054, 10103, 10415, 11138 and 11303 at their own rows, so the whole family was swept by the same sentence on the same date. (3) The OFR note 'See: Transfer Order 40 of the Secretary of Defense dated July 22, 1949 (14 FR 4908)' is a cross-reference (edge LE-6bdb8b3573f1 is typed cross_reference); a departmental transfer order cannot amend or end an executive order and it does not name EO 10054; ruled out, not a later event. The dossier's machine 'termination' lead (EO 10054 against EO 9721, edge LE-f1e26f42aee9) is the order's own modifying sentence, not an end. (4) Statutory leads (Federal Employees International Organization Service Act, 72 Stat. 961, cited in EO 10804) are not held beyond that citation and are not express ends. The dossier has no missing lines and no conflicts. Later events attached: none, because none ends or changes this clause. Savings: transferred_or_accrued (see savings reason). Risk noted for the reviewer: a spent-by-exhaustion reading (window closed by 1954) would make EO 12553 only an upper bound; no source shows the exhaustion date, so the express revocation is used.

Reading record LSP-EO_12553 (ending instrument): one operative sentence ('to eliminate Executive Orders that are no longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked:') followed by a No./Subject table and the signature block 'THE WHITE HOUSE, February 25, 1986.'; it has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25 (the on_signing reading; Federal Register publication on 1986-03-03 is not an effective date); it has no savings, continuation, transfer, exception or delayed-effect provision. Own-residual check, reading EO 10054 in full: it creates no office, function, fund or property and sets no continuing duty. Its only substantive effect is a personal, conditional entitlement: Gerald C. Gross, if his Union service ends 'without prejudice within five years' of its beginning (before 1949-04-29, so by 1954-04-29 at the latest) and he meets the other conditions of EO 9721, 'shall be entitled to such reemployment rights'. Whether his service ended in that window and whether he was reemployed is unheld. Any right that vested when his service ended in the window is an effect of the order that EO 12553 (which saves nothing) does not undo and that EO 10804 sec. 2 itself preserved for rights 'vested under each such order'; the later employment status would rest on civil-service law, not on this order. S0 prefill (none_after_bounded_search) OVERRULED to transferred_or_accrued because of the conditional personal reemployment right; the accrual itself cannot be shown from held sources, which is why the state is recorded and not 'none'. Bounded search: every held official FR text under jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts (6,652 files) was grepped for the order's number, its subject words and the generic-reference phrases that could change it; the OFR catalog edges (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv, COUNTEREVIDENCE_LEADS.csv, UNPARSED_NOTE_SEGMENTS.csv), the dossier's current-law leads (none) and the three machine searches were read.

EO 10134 (June 28, 1950) further extended the committee for four years from June 30, 1950 to June 30, 1954. The Quetico-Superior Committee was created by EO 6783 (1934) for a limited period and kept alive by successive four-year extension orders (EOs 7921, 9213, 9741, 10134, 10541, 10767, 11031) and amended by EOs 9890, 10589 and 11031. EO 11342 of April 10, 1967 (32 FR 5827) established a committee of the same name anew (sec. 1), let it carry forward the old committee's uncompleted business (sec. 5) and in sec. 6 superseded EO 6783 and all nine continuing or amending orders; it states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. That supersession was a formal cleanup: each extension order had already run out on the fixed date it states, and the last extension (EO 11031 sec. 1) ended on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification disposition row for EO 6783 lists no continuation after EO 11031, the OFR catalog has no Quetico order between EO 11031 and EO 11342, and EO 11342 establishes the committee anew, so the committee lapsed on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification ('Superseded by EO 11342') and the OFR catalog note were used only as leads; the dates come from the order texts. Texts were checked against the text layer of the saved official Federal Register scans (fr-originals); no page-image comparison was made. This order's only operative provision is the extension itself, so its operation ended on 1954-06-30; the 1967 supersession is recorded as a later event.

Neither this order nor EO 11342 contains a savings clause preserving any provision of this order. EO 11342 sec. 5 lets the new committee carry forward uncompleted business and succeed to records and property of the committee provided for in EO 6783; that is a successor-order transition for the committee's affairs, not a continuation of this order's terms.

EO:10145 read in the FR machine text (original_representation_unverified, acceptable_as_original). The single operative paragraph extends enlistments that expire inside a dated window (enlistments expiring after 1950-07-27 and "prior to July 9, 1951"). The order stops reaching new expiries on the cutoff date 1951-07-09; the extensions granted before then persist to the dates in the savings note. EO 10270 (1951-07-06) takes the next window and excludes enlistments already extended by EO 10145 and EO 10164; it does not extend or amend EO 10145. EO 10358 of June 9, 1952 (official text 17 FR 5269, saved OCR text layer of the govinfo issue PDF read in full from heading to signature and filing line) sets holiday-observance rules for executive agencies: application (s.1), definitions of holiday and workday (s.2), closing of offices on the Monday after a Sunday holiday (s.3), next-workday and in-lieu rules for employees (ss.4-6), pay-and-leave treatment (s.7), and an effective date sixty days after signing with supersession of EO 9636 (s.8). EO 11226 (May 27, 1965, 30 FR 7213) rewrote section 7 and added a section 9 for employees on uncommon tours of duty, effective on issuance; EO 11272 (February 23, 1966, 31 FR 3111) rewrote section 1 and added a section 10 excluding the postal field service from sections 4-7 and 9, effective on issuance. These amendments modified but did not end any original clause (each rewritten clause kept its original rule), so they are recorded as later events, not first ends. EO 11582 of February 11, 1971 (36 FR 2957, read in full) section 8 revokes EO 10358 and the amendatory EOs 11226 and 11272, and section 9 makes the order 'effective as of January 1, 1971', so the revocation is effective 1971-01-01 (the same day the Monday-holiday statute moved several of the dates listed in section 2(a); nothing ended any clause earlier). The order has no expiry or condition. The eCFR conflict lead (7 CFR 800.0 still mentions 'Executive Order 10358, as amended' when explaining weekend holiday observance) was read: it is a stale descriptive cross-reference in a grain-inspection definition and cannot keep a revoked order operating; the operative rules are 5 U.S.C. 6103 and EO 11582, so the lead is resolved and does not contradict the NO status. Section 8 is inventoried in two quoted parts because the OCR fuses the footnote marker to the superseded order's number (the number would not be a valid order number as printed); the omitted token is the number of EO 9636, identified by its date and title. All clauses first ended 1971-01-01, which is the whole-order end. OCR quotations are exact copies of the held text and have not been compared with page images.

EO 11582 contains no savings or transition clause for EO 10358; it revokes it (with its amending orders 11226 and 11272) and prescribes its own holiday-observance rules, which are EO 11582's own provisions, not a continuation of EO 10358. EO 10358 created no fund, office, property or vested right: holiday excusals and the pay and leave treatment applied before 1971 were completed payroll administration. Section 8's supersession of EO 9636 was a completed disposition that EO 11582 does not reverse.

EO 10440 (March 31, 1953; 18 FR 1823-1824, read in the held govinfo scan) rewrote Civil Service Rule VI (secs. 6.1-6.6, creating Schedule C) and in sec. 2 directed the Commission to reclassify existing Schedule A and B positions, keeping them in place until it acted. Earlier events: EO 10463 (June 25, 1953) replaced sec. 6.4, so the original sec. 6.4 ended that day. The other Rule VI sections continued until EO 10577 sec. 301 revoked EO 10440 by name, effective (sec. 401) on the first Sunday after the sixtieth day after November 22, 1954, i.e. January 23, 1955, which is therefore the whole-order end (no later-ending clause exists). Sec. 2 is a transitional direction that was spent once the Commission had reclassified every listed position; the date that happened is not in the held sources, so its first end is left open rather than set to the revocation date. Savings: EO 10577's proviso carried the schedule listings into the new rules.

EO 10577 sec. 301 attaches a proviso to its revocations: positions listed in Schedules A, B and C 'as provided for in Civil Service Rule VI of that order, as amended' (that is, Rule VI as rewritten by EO 10440, which created Schedule C) 'shall be considered as being listed in Schedules A, B, and C, respectively,' of the new Rule VI, unless and until the Commission removes them. The Commission's schedule placements made under EO 10440 were therefore carried into EO 10577's schedules; they continue, if at all, under EO 10577 and later rules, not under EO 10440. No other savings clause was found.

EO 10529 (April 22, 1954; 19 FR 2397) was read in the held official FR scan (fr-originals OCR of PDF pages 1-3: heading, enacting clause, sections 1-5, Eisenhower signature and FR Doc. 54-3141). Section 2 begins on page 2397 and continues on page 2399 after the issue's contents pages; the clause is quoted from page 2399. Operative clauses: the Administrator's recommendation of volunteer Federal personnel for State and local pre-emergency civil-defense training (sec. 1); the agency head's year-to-year authorization (sec. 2) and its three conditions (sec. 2(a)-(c)); continued pay, status and travel (sec. 3); a construction rule (sec. 4); and two definitions (sec. 5). There is no expiry, condition or report duty. Later events, read in the held texts: EO 10773 (July 1, 1958), EO 10782 (effective August 26, 1958, renaming the office in EO 10773's substituted references) and EO 11051 section 603(d) (September 27, 1962) only substituted the responsible officials (ODCM/OCDM Director, then OEP Director or Secretary of Defense); they are amendments, not ends. Section 1's reference to section 3 of EO 10346 describes the arrangements the recommendations serve; EO 10346 was revoked by EO 11490 in 1969, but section 1 does not make its own authority depend on EO 10346, and EO 10529 was still being maintained by amendment, so that revocation is not treated as an end. EO 12148 (signed July 20, 1979; 44 FR 43239, held) section 5-104 revokes EO 10529, as amended, and section 6 makes the order effective July 15, 1979; that stated effective date is the first end of every clause and the whole-order end. The OFR catalog and the 1989 OFR Codification disposition table (amended by EOs 10773, 11051; revoked by EO 12148) agree. The current-law machine hits for this order are U.S. Code editorial notes recording its amendments and its revocation by EO 12148, not a continuing basis. No other amendment, revocation or statute affecting EO 10529 was found in the bounded searches listed.

EO 12148 revokes EO 10529 outright. Its only transition rule, section 2-302, lets the FEMA Director continue to perform functions transferred to him by section 1 of EO 12148 notwithstanding the revocations; that is a continuation of FEMA's own transferred functions, not a saving of EO 10529's terms, and EO 12148 does not re-enact the 40-hour limit or the other conditions of EO 10529. EO 10529 authorized time-limited training assignments while employees stayed in Federal pay status; it created no vested rights, and pay or travel already allowed for past assignments were completed. No surviving effect traceable to EO 10529 was found.

EO 10541 (June 30, 1954) further extended the committee for four years from June 30, 1954 to June 30, 1958. The Quetico-Superior Committee was created by EO 6783 (1934) for a limited period and kept alive by successive four-year extension orders (EOs 7921, 9213, 9741, 10134, 10541, 10767, 11031) and amended by EOs 9890, 10589 and 11031. EO 11342 of April 10, 1967 (32 FR 5827) established a committee of the same name anew (sec. 1), let it carry forward the old committee's uncompleted business (sec. 5) and in sec. 6 superseded EO 6783 and all nine continuing or amending orders; it states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. That supersession was a formal cleanup: each extension order had already run out on the fixed date it states, and the last extension (EO 11031 sec. 1) ended on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification disposition row for EO 6783 lists no continuation after EO 11031, the OFR catalog has no Quetico order between EO 11031 and EO 11342, and EO 11342 establishes the committee anew, so the committee lapsed on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification ('Superseded by EO 11342') and the OFR catalog note were used only as leads; the dates come from the order texts. Texts were checked against the text layer of the saved official Federal Register scans (fr-originals); no page-image comparison was made. This order's only operative provision is the extension itself, so its operation ended on 1958-06-30; the 1967 supersession is recorded as a later event.

Neither this order nor EO 11342 contains a savings clause preserving any provision of this order. EO 11342 sec. 5 lets the new committee carry forward uncompleted business and succeed to records and property of the committee provided for in EO 6783; that is a successor-order transition for the committee's affairs, not a continuation of this order's terms.

EO 10559 (Sept. 8, 1954; 19 FR 5879) has two operative sections: sec. 1 delegates to the Budget Director the President's authority to allocate the 'Expenses of Management Improvement' appropriation (and any reenactment); sec. 2 requires reports and direction of the funded activities. Neither section has an expiry or condition; the delegation follows the paragraph as reenacted, and EO 11230 sec. 1(23) itself delegates the paragraph as reenacted in the Executive Office Appropriation Act 1965, so the authority was still live in 1965. No amendment of EO 10559 is recorded in the OFR catalog edges or the 1989 Codification disposition table ('Superseded by EO 11230'). EO 11230 sec. 2(2) expressly supersedes EO 10559; EO 11230 states no effective date and so took effect on issuance, June 28, 1965. Both clauses therefore first ended on 1965-06-28, which is also the whole-order end. Savings: EO 11230 sec. 4 keeps prior actions and regulations in effect under EO 11230 and sec. 3(b) redirects references; the function itself passes to EO 11230 sec. 1(23). No current-law citation of EO 10559 was found (U.S. Code release 119-121, eCFR as of 2026-10-14).

EO 11230 sec. 4 keeps in effect all actions taken and regulations prescribed or approved in the matters covered by its sec. 1 (which re-delegates the same presidential functions to the Director of the Bureau of the Budget) until amended or revoked under EO 11230; sec. 3(b) redirects references to superseded orders to the corresponding provision of EO 11230. The functions therefore pass to EO 11230 and past actions survive under it; nothing continues to rest on this order. EO 11230 sec. 1(23) re-delegates the same management-improvement allocation authority (as reenacted) and the same reporting and direction duty.

EO 10697 of February 6, 1957 (22 FR 777, read in full) prescribes a new Tariff of Fees and in section 7 revokes 'No. 10,639 of October 10,1955' among the earlier tariff orders, 'To the extent that they have not heretofore been revoked or superseded', effective March 1, 1957 (section 8). The order has no expiry or condition and no earlier amendment or revocation was found in the OFR catalog, the saved-text corpus or the U.S. Code/eCFR searches. EO 10697 contains no savings or transition clause. It prescribes a complete new Tariff of Fees and its own collection rules (sections 1-6), effective March 1, 1957, and revokes the earlier tariff orders to the extent not already revoked or superseded. Fees charged under the earlier tariff were completed transactions; the order created no fund, office, property or vested right that survived. The deletion of Items 1-5 was overtaken by the new Tariff, which is EO 10697's own schedule.

Executive Order 10645 (official Federal Register text, 20 FR 8681, PDF pages 1-1, read in the saved OCR text layer of the govinfo issue PDF: heading, enacting clause, operative text and signature/filing line are all present) permits a federal officer or employee to hold the office of Member of the State Board of Agriculture of Michigan, with a non-interference proviso. Its whole operative content is an amendment of Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873, as amended (the 1989 OFR disposition table: 'Amended EO 9'; 'Revoked by EO 11408'). EO 11408 of April 25, 1968 (33 FR 6459, saved official text read in full) revoked EO 9 itself in section 1 and in section 2 revoked 'All prior Executive orders insofar as they interpret or amend Executive Order No. 9'; EO 11408 section 2 names it expressly in its list of revoked amendatory orders. Because the order consists only of that amendment, 'insofar as' reaches all of it, which is also why the OFR catalog's '(in part)' qualifier on some of these notes does not leave any part in force. EO 11408 states no effective date, so the revocation took effect on signing, 1968-04-25. No earlier end was found: the order has no expiry, condition or temporary term, the OFR catalog and the saved-text corpus show no earlier amendment or revocation, and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches show no current citation. Each clause therefore first ended on 1968-04-25 and that is the whole-order end. OCR quotations keep the scan's recognition errors (and soft hyphens) exactly as held; they have not been compared with page images.

EO 11408 contains no savings, transition or continuation clause. Its section 1 revoked Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873 (the dual federal-state office-holding prohibition) itself, and section 2 revoked every prior order insofar as it interpreted or amended that order. This order's only operative content is an amendment of (an exception to) that 1873 order, so once the prohibition itself was revoked nothing remained for the exception to operate on, and no office, fund, property, entitlement or enforceable right was created by the order that could survive; office-holding done under the permission before 1968 was lawful when done and is a completed historical fact, not a continuing effect.

The order's only time term is tied to section 407(b) remaining in force; EO 11230 sec. 1(22) re-delegates the same section 407(b) authority in 1965, which shows the statute had not ceased by then, so no earlier ending applies. EO 11230 sec. 2(4) supersedes EO 10766, effective on issuance June 28, 1965; all three clauses and the order first ended on 1965-06-28. Savings pass to EO 11230 under its secs. 3(b) and 4. No current-law citation was found.

EO 11230 sec. 4 keeps in effect all actions taken and regulations prescribed or approved in the matters covered by its sec. 1 (which re-delegates the same presidential functions to the Director of the Bureau of the Budget) until amended or revoked under EO 11230; sec. 3(b) redirects references to superseded orders to the corresponding provision of EO 11230. The functions therefore pass to EO 11230 and past actions survive under it; nothing continues to rest on this order. EO 11230 sec. 1(22) re-delegates the same section 407(b) approval authority and the same reporting requirement under section 407(c).

EO 10767 (May 9, 1958) further extended the committee for a period of four years ending June 30, 1962. The Quetico-Superior Committee was created by EO 6783 (1934) for a limited period and kept alive by successive four-year extension orders (EOs 7921, 9213, 9741, 10134, 10541, 10767, 11031) and amended by EOs 9890, 10589 and 11031. EO 11342 of April 10, 1967 (32 FR 5827) established a committee of the same name anew (sec. 1), let it carry forward the old committee's uncompleted business (sec. 5) and in sec. 6 superseded EO 6783 and all nine continuing or amending orders; it states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. That supersession was a formal cleanup: each extension order had already run out on the fixed date it states, and the last extension (EO 11031 sec. 1) ended on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification disposition row for EO 6783 lists no continuation after EO 11031, the OFR catalog has no Quetico order between EO 11031 and EO 11342, and EO 11342 establishes the committee anew, so the committee lapsed on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification ('Superseded by EO 11342') and the OFR catalog note were used only as leads; the dates come from the order texts. Texts were checked against the text layer of the saved official Federal Register scans (fr-originals); no page-image comparison was made. This order's only operative provision is the extension itself, so its operation ended on 1962-06-30; the 1967 supersession is recorded as a later event.

Neither this order nor EO 11342 contains a savings clause preserving any provision of this order. EO 11342 sec. 5 lets the new committee carry forward uncompleted business and succeed to records and property of the committee provided for in EO 6783; that is a successor-order transition for the committee's affairs, not a continuation of this order's terms.

EO 10880 (June 7, 1960; 25 FR 5131, held official FR scan text) allowed indefinite and temporary employees meeting stated service conditions to have their appointments converted to career or career-conditional appointments. Six operative clauses are quoted verbatim (Sec. 1(a) with its conditions (i)-(v), Sec. 1(b) postal substitutes, Sec. 2 definitions, Sec. 3 returning service members, Sec. 4 exclusions, Sec. 5 rule-making). The order's own terms close the agency-recommendation window for Sec. 1(a) one year after its date, but set no date by which conversions had to be completed (Sec. 1(b) conversions wait for career substitute vacancies), and Sec. 3 stays open for any qualifying service member re-employed after discharge; no earlier cessation can therefore be proved from the order itself, and the recommendation deadline is not treated as an end. EO 12107 (effective January 1, 1979) redesignated the Civil Service Commission as the Office of Personnel Management in this order, confirming it was still treated as in force. EO 12608 of September 9, 1987, Sec. 1, revoked it (no separate effective date), which is the first end of every clause and the whole-order end; the same section preserves 'benefits already conferred'. USC note at 5 U.S.C. 3301 and the OFR 1989 table agree.

EO 12608 Sec. 1 expressly provides that, notwithstanding the revocation of EO 10880, benefits already conferred under it before revocation shall not be affected: appointments already converted to career or career-conditional status stand. No new conversion could be made under the order after September 9, 1987.

EO 10889 (Oct. 5, 1960; 25 FR 9633) adds paragraphs (p), (q) and (r) to section 1 (Part I) of EO 10530 and, in sec. 2, supersedes four 1960 presidential letters under Alaska Omnibus Act sec. 45(a). Clause by clause: (p)(1), the determination power under sec. 45(a), ran until EO 11164 substituted the whole of paragraph (p) on Aug. 1, 1964 (EO 11164 states no effective date; effective on issuance). (p)(2), the conveyance power, was delegated only 'until July 1, 1964' by this order's own words, so it first ended on 1964-07-01 by its own terms, before EO 11164 restored a conveyance power without that limit. (q) was replaced in full by EO 10960 on Aug. 21, 1961 (substitution 'to read as follows', effective on issuance). Sec. 2's supersession of the four letters was completed on issuance, Oct. 5, 1960 (spent; recorded as its first end). (r) and the enacting words continued until EO 11230 sec. 2 superseded Part I of EO 10530 (item 1) and EO 10889 (item 7), effective on issuance June 28, 1965. Convention: a clause whose whole text is replaced by a later order's substituted text ends on that order's effective date; the substituted text is the later order's clause. A first_end that is a limit in the order itself uses the first day the clause no longer applied. Whole-order end = latest clause end = 1965-06-28. The OFR catalog also records EO 10960 as amending this order; the 1989 Codification row reads 'Amended EO 10530. Amended by EO 10960 ... Superseded by EO 11230'. The only current-law hit is the 3 U.S.C. 301 note's status line for EO 10530 ('as amended by ... Ex. Ord. No. ...'), an amendment history of the host order, not a current predicate for this order; the provisions it added to section 1 (Part I) of EO 10530 were superseded with Part I by EO 11230 sec. 2(1). The clause inventory is quoted from the official FR scan (the draft's clauses came from a mirror transcription and were not used).

EO 11230 sec. 4 keeps in effect all actions taken and regulations prescribed or approved in the matters covered by its sec. 1 (which re-delegates the same presidential functions to the Director of the Bureau of the Budget) until amended or revoked under EO 11230; sec. 3(b) redirects references to superseded orders to the corresponding provision of EO 11230. The functions therefore pass to EO 11230 and past actions survive under it; nothing continues to rest on this order. Sec. 2 of this order superseded four presidential letters 'without prejudice to any action heretofore taken'; that completed supersession is not undone by EO 11230. EO 11230 sec. 1(27)-(28) re-delegates the Alaska sec. 45(a) and Hawaii sec. 5(e) authorities; the Hawaii Omnibus Act sec. 40 procedures authority in paragraph (r) is not re-delegated and simply ends.

EO 10898 (December 2, 1960; 25 FR 12429, read in the held govinfo scan) established the Interdepartmental Highway Safety Board of cabinet officers (sec. 1), gave it coordinating and study functions (sec. 2), provided agency assistance (sec. 3), made it advisory only (sec. 4) and required reports (sec. 5). It has no term of its own. Earlier clause-level ends: EO 10986 (January 12, 1962) substituted a new sec. 1(b), so the original membership list ended then; EO 11382 sec. 8 (November 28, 1967) struck all of sec. 1(b) as amended and changed the quorum in sec. 1(d) from three to four, so the original quorum rule ended then. EO 11382 sec. 16(3) also revoked EO 10858, which sec. 4 cites for the President's Committee for Traffic Safety; this is recorded as a later event on sec. 4, but the section's main rule (Board advisory only) continued. EO 11515 (March 13, 1970) terminated the Board and revoked EO 10898 and EO 10986 without a stated effective date, so the remaining clauses ended on March 13, 1970, the whole-order end. EO 11031 (June 19, 1962) extended the committee for four years ending June 30, 1966 (sec. 1), re-appointed its three appointive members for a four-year period ending the same day (sec. 2(a)), continued the two designated members at the Secretaries' pleasure (sec. 2(b)) and amended EO 6783 accordingly (sec. 3). The Quetico-Superior Committee was created by EO 6783 (1934) for a limited period and kept alive by successive four-year extension orders (EOs 7921, 9213, 9741, 10134, 10541, 10767, 11031) and amended by EOs 9890, 10589 and 11031. EO 11342 of April 10, 1967 (32 FR 5827) established a committee of the same name anew (sec. 1), let it carry forward the old committee's uncompleted business (sec. 5) and in sec. 6 superseded EO 6783 and all nine continuing or amending orders; it states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. That supersession was a formal cleanup: each extension order had already run out on the fixed date it states, and the last extension (EO 11031 sec. 1) ended on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification disposition row for EO 6783 lists no continuation after EO 11031, the OFR catalog has no Quetico order between EO 11031 and EO 11342, and EO 11342 establishes the committee anew, so the committee lapsed on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification ('Superseded by EO 11342') and the OFR catalog note were used only as leads; the dates come from the order texts. Texts were checked against the text layer of the saved official Federal Register scans (fr-originals); no page-image comparison was made. Secs. 1 and 2(a) ended by their own terms on June 30, 1966; secs. 2(b) and 3 had no term of their own and ceased with the committee that day. The draft's EVENT_BEFORE_SIGNING conflicts came from a catalog note listing earlier extensions (EOs 10134, 10541, 10589, 10767) that predate and do not affect this order. Whole-order end: 1966-06-30.

Neither this order nor EO 11342 contains a savings clause preserving any provision of this order. EO 11342 sec. 5 lets the new committee carry forward uncompleted business and succeed to records and property of the committee provided for in EO 6783; that is a successor-order transition for the committee's affairs, not a continuation of this order's terms.

EO 11112 (June 12, 1963; 28 FR 6037-6038) establishes the President's Advisory Council on the Arts: establishment (1(a)), composition and terms (1(b)), chairman (1(c)), compensation (1(d)), meetings (1(e)), functions (2(a)(1)-(5)), hearing interested parties (2(b)), definition of the arts (2(c)), and agency liaison, information, assistance and GSA services (3(a)-(d)). No expiry or condition. EO 11124 (Oct. 28, 1963) substituted a new subsection (b) of Section 1 (two more ex officio members, up to forty private members), so the original 1(b) first ended on 1963-10-28 (convention: wholesale substitution ends the original clause; the new text is EO 11124's own clause). The National Council on the Arts Act of Sept. 3, 1964 did not itself abolish the Council; EO 11208 recites that it 'obviat[ed] the need' and then revokes EO 11112 and EO 11124, effective on issuance Mar. 24, 1965 (signature date garbled in the OCR; filing line Mar. 25, 1965 and OFR catalog Mar. 24, 1965). All other clauses first ended on 1965-03-24, the whole-order end. Whether private members were appointed before the Council's work was overtaken by the 1964 statute was not established from the bounded sources; the clauses' legal operation (the Council existed from the order, with ex officio federal members by office, and EO 11124 sec. 2 refers to sitting members) ran to the revocation, and no earlier presidential or statutory act ending the Council was found in the OFR catalog or the saved texts. 1989 Codification row: 'Amended by EO 11124 ... Revoked by EO 11208'. No current-law citation.

EO 11208 has no savings or transfer clause. Its preamble records that the National Council on the Arts, established by the Act of Sept. 3, 1964 (P.L. 88-579), obviated the need for the President's Council; that statutory council is an independent body, not a continuation of this order, and no function, property or right is transferred to it by EO 11208. The Council's advisory functions simply ended; compensation and travel expenses of private members for days served were paid under the general statute cited (5 U.S.C. 55a, 73b-2), not under a continuing obligation of the order.

EO 11117 (August 13, 1963; 28 FR 8397-8398, read in the held govinfo scan) established an Interagency Committee on International Athletics of agency representatives, with information-gathering and reporting functions (secs. 1-3). It has no term or condition of its own, no amendment is recorded (OFR catalog; 1989 Codification table, a lead), and it ended before the Federal Advisory Committee Act (1972) existed, so no statutory termination applies. EO 11515 sec. 2 terminated the Committee and revoked EO 11117 without a stated effective date, so every clause ended on March 13, 1970.

EO 11515 sec. 6 assigns the winding up of outstanding affairs of the bodies it terminates to the Bureau of the Budget (or agencies its Director designates). Only residual affairs were transferred for winding up; no function, right or obligation of the Committee was continued, and EO 11117 itself has no savings provision.

EO 11152 (April 15, 1964; 29 FR 5271-5272, read in the held govinfo scan) established the President's Committee on Manpower of cabinet and agency heads to assist the Secretary of Labor under the Manpower Development and Training Act (secs. 1-4). It has no term or condition of its own, no amendment is recorded (OFR catalog; 1989 Codification table, a lead), and it ended before the Federal Advisory Committee Act (1972) existed, so no statutory termination applies. EO 11515 sec. 3 terminated the Committee and revoked EO 11152 without a stated effective date, so every clause ended on March 13, 1970. Winding up went to the Bureau of the Budget (sec. 6).

EO 11515 sec. 6 assigns the winding up of outstanding affairs of the bodies it terminates to the Bureau of the Budget (or agencies its Director designates). Only residual affairs were transferred for winding up. EO 11152 sec. 4 left all statutory functions (including the Secretary of Labor's under the Manpower Development and Training Act) where the law placed them, so nothing depended on the Committee's existence.

EO 11482 (September 22, 1969; 34 FR 14723-14725, read in the held govinfo scan) created a tripartite Construction Industry Collective Bargaining Commission with study, recommendation, dispute-intercession, rule-making and reporting functions (secs. 1-9). Clause inventory from the official scan, with each provision quoted from one page. EO 12110 sec. 1-103(a) revoked it effective December 31, 1978 (sec. 1-105) as one whose committee had 'terminated' or whose work was 'completed', so the revocation is likely a clean-up after an earlier end. The candidate earlier end is statutory: under Federal Advisory Committee Act sec. 14(a)(1), advisory committees in existence on January 5, 1973 terminated on January 5, 1975 unless renewed, and EO 11827 sec. 4 says the same of presidential committees it did not continue; EO 11827 did not continue this Commission. Whether the Act reached this body, which mediated and intervened in disputes as well as advising, is a legal question left open, so first ends are not asserted. The CONFLICT (29 CFR part 901 still cites the order) is left open because the eCFR text is not on this machine.

EO 11534 (June 4, 1970; 35 FR 8865, read in the held govinfo scan) created a National Council on Organized Crime of eighteen named federal officials to formulate a national strategy against organized crime. It has no term, report deadline or condition, and no amendment is recorded (OFR catalog; 1989 Codification table, a lead). EO 12110 sec. 1-103(c) lists it among orders 'that established committees which have terminated or whose work is completed'. That recital gives no date and is not itself a legal act ending the Council earlier; the order's own terms set no end, and the Council, composed wholly of full-time federal officers, was outside the termination rule of sec. 14 of the Federal Advisory Committee Act (the continuance orders EO 11827 and EO 11948 accordingly do not list it). The legal first end of every clause is therefore the revocation, effective December 31, 1978 under sec. 1-105. Changes in some members' offices (for example the Post Office Department and the Bureau of Narcotics and Dangerous Drugs were later reorganized) altered who sat on the Council but did not end it; they were not separately researched.

EO 12110 revokes EO 11534 with no savings or winding-up clause. EO 11534 only created a coordinating council of federal officials charged with formulating a strategy; it conferred no right, benefit, office or obligation on any person, and the members' own statutory law-enforcement functions never depended on it. Nothing of the order was found to survive.

Family method: the researcher read the saved official Federal Register OCR text layers (heading to FR Doc line) of this order, of EO 11248 and of all 40 orders that the OFR disposition notes and the 1989 Codification list as amending it, plus EO 11708, 11715, 11736 and 11768, and traced every item of EO 11248 sections 1 and 2 through each addition, deletion, word substitution and renumbering. Where a later amender deletes an item and inserts another in its place, the earlier item's placement ends on that amender's effective date; the series' separate 'substituting for the words' formula is treated as a retitling that continues the item. Abolition of a position by unpublished departmental action is outside the held sources and is a limitation of this bounded search. Page images were not viewed; quotations are exact from the saved OCR, including its recognition errors. No human certification is asserted.

EO 11641 (January 28, 1972) had the Attorney General establish an Office for Drug Abuse Law Enforcement in the Department of Justice (sec. 1(a)), headed by a Director with the title Special Assistant Attorney General (sec. 1(b)) who also served as Special Consultant to the President (sec. 1(c)) and ran a concentrated federal enforcement program (sec. 1(d)); required consultation with the Special Action Office for Drug Abuse Prevention (sec. 2); placed the Director in level IV by amending EO 11248 sec. 1 (sec. 3); and required agency assistance (sec. 4). EO 11727 of July 6, 1973 (38 FR 18357) recites that Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1973, effective July 1, 1973, establishes the Drug Enforcement Administration into which both offices' functions would be merged; it revokes EO 11641 (sec. 2) and EO 11676 (sec. 3), directs the Attorney General to reassign their functions, abolish the offices and wind up their affairs (secs. 2, 3, 5), deletes both directors from level IV as listed in EO 11708 (sec. 4), and is 'effective as of July 1, 1973' (sec. 6). First_end uses that stated effective date, not the July 6 signing date. One earlier partial end (also noted by the OFR catalog, which records EO 11248 as revoked by EO 11708): sec. 3 of this order had inserted its director into EO 11248 sec. 1, and EO 11708 sec. 3 (March 23, 1973) revoked EO 11248 as amended except for level V positions, so sec. 3 ended on 1973-03-23 (EO 11708 sec. 1 placed the director anew, and EO 11727 sec. 4 later deleted that placement). The U.S. Code note under 21 U.S.C. 801 (release point 119-121), which reprints EO 11727, and the eCFR hits were read: they record the revocation and nothing continuing. The 1989 Codification disposition table and the OFR catalog note were used as leads only; the dates come from the order texts, checked against the text layer of the saved official FR scans (no page-image comparison). EO 11667 (April 19, 1972; 37 FR 7763) was read in the held official Federal Register scan (fr-originals OCR of PDF pages 7-8: heading, preamble, sections 1-3, signature block and FR Doc. 72-6171 filing line, so the text is complete). Its operative content is the establishment and composition of the President's Advisory Committee on the Environmental Merit Awards Program (sec. 1(a)), three committee functions (sec. 1(b)), the no-compensation/travel-expense rule (sec. 2) and EPA administrative support (sec. 3); the preamble is narrative. The order has no expiry, sunset, report deadline or condition. Because the committee existed before the Federal Advisory Committee Act took effect (January 5, 1973), it would have terminated on January 5, 1975 unless renewed; EO 11827 section 1(8) (held, 40 FR 1218) renewed it until January 5, 1977. Before that date EO 11948 (held, 41 FR 55706) section 4(a)(1) revoked EO 11667, and section 5 makes EO 11948 effective December 31, 1976; section 3's separate January 16, 1977 date applies only to EO 11868. So the first and only end of every clause is the revocation effective December 31, 1976, and the whole-order end is that date. The OFR catalog (revoked by EO 11948; continued by EO 11827) and the 1989 OFR Codification disposition table (continued by EO 11827; revoked by EO 11948) agree, and no other amendment, revocation or statute affecting the order was found in the bounded searches listed (no U.S. Code or eCFR citation of the order). Quotations are the scan's OCR text, kept as printed (soft hyphens at line ends).

EO 11948 revokes EO 11667 without any saving or transition clause (its only other provisions continue a different list of committees, delegate FACA functions for those committees, revoke other orders and supersede EO 11827). EO 11667 created an advisory committee, its award-selection function, an uncompensated-service rule with travel expenses, and EPA administrative support; it conferred no vested rights or continuing obligations. Awards already conferred were completed honorary acts. The Environmental Merit Awards Program itself was announced by the President in 1971 (EO 11667 preamble) and was not created by this order; any later EPA award activity rests on EPA's own authority and is not attributed to EO 11667.

Family method: the researcher read the saved official Federal Register OCR text layers (heading to FR Doc line) of this order, of EO 11248 and of all 40 orders that the OFR disposition notes and the 1989 Codification list as amending it, plus EO 11708, 11715, 11736 and 11768, and traced every item of EO 11248 sections 1 and 2 through each addition, deletion, word substitution and renumbering. Pure deletions, renumberings and effective-date provisions are one-time edits completed when the order took effect. The 5 U.S.C. 5315-5316 amendment notes for 1964-1973 record no statutory placement of the positions concerned. EO 11756 (signed Dec. 30, 1973; 39 FR 781, Jan. 3, 1974), read in full in the held FR text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11756.txt), is a single-clause order under 5 U.S.C. 8335(c) exempting Whitney Gillilland, Vice Chairman of the Civil Aeronautics Board, from mandatory retirement for age 'until December 31, 1974'. It is a fixed-term grant that ends by its own terms on 1974-12-31 (TERM record own_terms_until_event, chars 1017-1267). The only later order naming him is EO 11824 (signed Dec. 28, 1974; 40 FR 751), which I read in full from the held actor text: it recites that Mr. Gillilland 'was exempted through December 31, 1974, by Executive Order No. 11756 and has continued to serve on the Civil Aeronautics Board during 1974', finds the public interest requires that he 'continue to be exempted', and issues a fresh exemption 'until June 30, 1975' under the same subsection. It does not amend, extend or revoke EO 11756, and it positively confirms that the exemption ran its full term (no early departure). Searches: OFR catalog lists no disposition note on either order; U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches have 0 hits; my own scan of held FR order texts and APP texts for 'Gillilland' finds only EO 11756 and EO 11824. Authority check: 5 U.S.C. 8335(c) is the statutory basis cited in both orders; no held source shows its repeal before the stated end.

EO 11768 (February 20, 1974) placed 16 positions in level IV (sec. 1) and 9 in level V (sec. 2), protected incumbents (sec. 3) and superseded EO 11708 (sec. 4). EO 11861 of May 21, 1975 (40 FR 22531) placed a new complete list of positions in levels IV and V of the Executive Schedule and in sec. 4 superseded 'Executive Order No. 11768 of February 20, 1974, as amended'; it states no effective date for itself (the only dates in it are the June 1, 1975 termination of one listed position), so it took effect on signing. The amending orders EOs 11774 (March 26, 1974), 11780 (April 22, 1974), 11831 (January 9, 1975) and 11843 (March 18, 1975, effective March 1, 1975) operated only as text inserted into EO 11768, so the supersession of EO 11768 'as amended' ended them too, except where an amendment had already been displaced. The 1989 Codification ('Superseded by EO 11861') and the OFR catalog notes were used as leads only; every date comes from the order texts, checked against the text layer of the saved official FR scans (no page-image comparison). Item-level ends: sec. 1(7) was replaced by EO 11774 on March 26, 1974; sec. 1(3), (12) and (15) were replaced and sec. 1(16) deleted by EO 11831 on January 9, 1975; every other placement, both lead-ins and sec. 3 ended with the supersession on May 21, 1975. Sec. 4 (supersession of EO 11708) was a one-time act complete on issuance. EO 11780's addition of sec. 2(10) is recorded as a later event on sec. 2. The draft's STATED_EFFECTIVE_DATE_DIFFERS conflicts are resolved: EO 11831 has no stated effective date (its 'March 1, 1975' is the termination date of the position it inserted) and EO 11843 is effective March 1, 1975. Whole-order end: 1975-05-21.

EO 11809 (September 30, 1974; 39 FR 35565) was read in the held official FR scan (fr-originals OCR of PDF page 15, heading to FR Doc. 74-23127). Its five operative sections establish the President's Labor-Management Committee (eight labor, eight management members and a neutral coordinator), state its study-and-advice functions, direct it to encourage sector labor-management committees, direct agency cooperation and assign FACA functions to the Treasury. EO 11948 (held) section 4(a)(2) revokes it, effective December 31, 1976 under section 5. EO 11832 (January 9, 1975; 40 FR 2415-2417, read in the held govinfo scan) established the National Commission on the Observance of International Women's Year, 1975 (secs. 1-3) and an interdepartmental task force (sec. 4). Exact clause-level ends found: EO 11889 (November 25, 1975) replaced the original sec. 2(h), which had ended the Commission's work with 1975; EO 11979 (March 28, 1977) replaced the original sec. 1(b) membership rule (further amended by EO 11980). The other clauses are certainly terminated by the cutoff, since EO 12050 sec. 8 revoked EO 11832 as amended on April 4, 1978, but that revocation may be a clean-up. Under EO 11889 the Commission was to end after a final report due within thirty days after June 30, 1976. EO 11979 shows it was still operating in 1977 'in accord with Section 2' of Public Law 94-167, which directed it to organize the National Women's Conference, and the Commission was set up after the Federal Advisory Committee Act took effect, so sec. 14(a)(2) of that Act also bears on its duration. Without reading Public Law 94-167, which states how long the Commission lasted and when it ended, the first ends of the Commission and task-force clauses, the whole-order end and the savings question cannot be fixed honestly; they are left open.

EO 11849 (April 1, 1975; 40 FR 14887-14888, read in the held govinfo scan) created the Collective Bargaining Committee in Construction (secs. 1-6). The order has no term of its own. EO 12110 sec. 1-103(b) revoked it effective December 31, 1978 as one whose committee had 'terminated' or whose work was 'completed', which signals an earlier end. The likely earlier end is the two-year limit of Federal Advisory Committee Act sec. 14(a)(2), since the general continuance order of December 1976 (EO 11948) did not renew it. Because the Act's application and the absence of any other renewal are not proven from held sources, first ends and the whole-order end are left open. Savings: none found. The U.S. Code note (29 U.S.C. 171 note) and the eCFR hits are historical and report the revocation; no CONFLICT is open.

EO 12110 revokes EO 11849 with no savings or winding-up clause. EO 11849 created a labor-management committee that facilitated bargaining and made recommendations; it conferred no right, benefit or obligation on any person and gave the Committee no binding power, so nothing was found that could survive its end, whenever that end occurred.

EO 11864 (June 13, 1975; 40 FR 25579) was read in the held official FR scan (fr-originals OCR of PDF page 11, complete from heading to FR Doc. 75-15839 and footnote). It is a single amending sentence: effective June 1, 1975, section 1 of EO 11861 (placing positions in level IV of the Executive Schedule) is revised at paragraph (13) to read 'Adviser to the Secretary (Counselor, Economic Policy Board), Department of the Treasury, to terminate effective August 1, 1975' (the OCR renders the closing '1975.”' with its footnote mark as '1,197571'; EO 11877 section 1(b), held, quotes the same paragraph with the date as 'August 1, 1975'). The order therefore fixed its own end: the placement lapsed on August 1, 1975, and that is the first end of the only clause and the whole-order end. The formal supersession came a month later: EO 11877 (September 2, 1975; 40 FR 40797, held), which states no effective date, superseded EO 11864 (section 2) and replaced paragraph (13) with an open-ended placement (section 1(b)); it is recorded as a later event, not as the first end, following the rule that a formal supersession can follow an earlier cessation under the order's own terms. A current-law note at 5 U.S.C. 5317 and the OFR catalog describe the same history (the note says the paragraph was 'to terminate effective August 1, 1975' and was superseded by EO 11877); the 1989 OFR Codification table lists EO 11864 as amending EO 11861 and superseded by EO 11877. The machine current-law hits for this order are that historical note, not a continuing basis.

EO 11864 has one operative provision: effective June 1, 1975 it revised paragraph (13) of section 1 of EO 11861 to place the Treasury Adviser (Counselor, Economic Policy Board) in level IV of the Executive Schedule, 'to terminate effective August 1, 1975'. The placement lapsed by its own terms on that date. EO 11877 later superseded EO 11864 and re-placed the position in level IV without a termination date; that later placement rests on EO 11877 (itself later revoked by EO 12076) and is not a residual of EO 11864. Neither order contains a saving clause. Pay earned at the level IV rate from June 1 to July 31, 1975 was a completed entitlement for that period, not a continuing effect; no continuing right or obligation traceable to EO 11864 was found.

EO 11868 (signed 1975-06-19, 40 FR 26255-26256), read in full from the held FR text, establishes the President's Commission on Olympic Sports (sec. 1), fixes its membership (sec. 2), directs a study of the United States Olympic Committee, impediments to fielding the best amateur athletes, financial support and related matters (sec. 3), requires two reports through the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare (sec. 4), lets the Chairman set up advisory committees (sec. 5), provides Health, Education, and Welfare support and funds (sec. 6), member pay and travel (sec. 7) and the FACA assignment (sec. 8). It has no term, sunset or termination-on-performance clause: the first report is due 'within five months after the Commission meets for the first time' and the second, as replaced by EO 11936, 'no later than January 15, 1977'; both are report deadlines and, under the project rule, never an end. EO 11873 (1975-07-21) replaces sec. 2 in full and EO 11936 (1976-09-08) replaces sec. 4(c) in full, each on signing; the original wording of those two clauses first ends on those dates and the replacement text runs to the revocation. EO 11948 sec. 3 revokes 'Executive Order No. 11868, as amended' 'effective January 16, 1977', the whole order and without qualifier, one day after the replacement report date; the twelve other original clauses first end on 1977-01-16 and the whole-order end is the latest first end, 1977-01-16. Checked and ruled out: no other held order names EO 11868; EO 11948 sec. 4(b) supersedes EO 11827, not this order; the dossier's STATED_EFFECTIVE_DATE_DIFFERS conflict is resolved for 1977-01-16; no FACA two-year termination applies because the order was revoked 1977-01-16 and a FACA committee created 1975-06-19 could run to 1977-06-19. Inventory: the recitals and the issuing paragraph were added to the dossier's fourteen operative clauses; trailing page furniture (sec. 3(c)) and the editorial note after sec. 8 were cut. A prior pilot decision for this order (research/production/claim-kit-pilot-2026-10-18/producer-11948) reached the same replacement-and-revocation reading; it was read as a lead only and the texts were re-read. Limitations: the dossier's fingerprint changed after selection (only chain.generic_refs_excluded 213 to 217) and the new dossier is used; the text is a machine-extracted official PDF text layer, not page images; the actual submission dates of the two reports and any earlier winding-up of the Commission are not known and are not asserted.

rationales.exact_text: Reading record instruments/readings/LSP-EO_11948.json (EO 11948, 41 FR 55705-55706, read once in full): sec. 3 revokes EO 11868 'as amended' effective 1977-01-16 with no savings, pending-matter or transition clause; sec. 2 reassigns Federal Advisory Committee Act functions only for the thirteen committees listed in sec. 1, which do not include the Commission; sec. 5 sets the general effective date. Own-residual check, reading EO 11868 in full (secs. 1-8): it created the Commission, its advisory committees, Health, Education, and Welfare support and expenses, member pay and travel and the FACA assignment, all of them dependent on the Commission; it revoked, transferred and funded nothing outside the Commission and created no private right. EO 11873 (sec. 2) and EO 11936 (sec. 4(c)) only replace two provisions. No successor delegation, transfer of functions or property, revival wording or continuing independent command was found. EO 12608 revoked the order on September 9, 1987 (later event), but that is probably a cleanup: the machine snippet of the 16 U.S.C. 1537a statutory note (the full note was not readable here) says 'but not later than 90 days after Dec. 28, 1979, the functions of the Commission be carried out by the Endangered Species Scientific Authority as established by Ex. EO 11948 (December 20, 1976, effective December 31, 1976) continued thirteen advisory committees until December 31, 1978 (sec. 1(a)-(m)), assigned the President's Federal Advisory Committee Act functions for them to the listed agency heads (sec. 2), revoked EO 11868 effective January 16, 1977 (sec. 3), revoked EOs 11667, 11809 and 11860 and superseded EO 11827 (sec. 4). Earlier partial ends found by reading the acting texts: EO 12007 (August 22, 1977) terminated the Citizens' Advisory Council on the Status of Women, the Citizens' Advisory Committee on Environmental Quality, the Advisory Council for Minority Enterprise and the Consumer Advisory Council and in sec. 6 superseded subsections (a), (g), (i) and (j) of sec. 1; EO 12029 (December 14, 1977) terminated the Quetico-Superior Committee and in sec. 2 superseded subsection (e). Neither states an effective date, so each took effect on signing. The remaining continuances ran 'until December 31, 1978', the same day EO 12110 (signed December 28, 1978) took effect under its sec. 1-105 and superseded this order (sec. 1-104); sec. 2 ended then too. Secs. 3, 4 and 5 were one-time acts complete on January 16, 1977 and December 31, 1976. The 1989 Codification disposition table and the OFR catalog note were used as leads only; the dates come from the order texts, checked against the text layer of the saved official FR scans (no page-image comparison). Whole-order end 1978-12-31.

No savings clause in EO 11948, EO 12007, EO 12029 or EO 12110 preserves a provision of this order. The committees that EO 12110 sec. 1-101 continued to December 31, 1980 were continued under EO 12110 itself; the committees terminated in 1977 were ended by EOs 12007 and 12029.

The machine own-term kinds are conditions (concurrence requirements in sec. 1(l)) and the 'until_event' wording of the sec. 4 proviso for EO 11501, none of which is an end of EO 11958; the order has no sunset or termination clause. EO 13637 (signed 2013-03-08, 78 FR 16129-16132, held FR text, read in full; reading record LSP-EO_13637) sec. 4 revokes it 'as amended' with no effective-date wording, so the revocation took effect on signing; the dossier's effective-date class 'unknown' is resolved from the text. Thirteen orders amended EO 11958 before that (EO 12118, 12163, 12210, 12321, 12365, 12423, 12560, 12680, 12738, 13030, 13091, 13118, 13284); the sections of each that amend EO 11958 were read in the held FR texts (several of these are omnibus orders whose other sections concern other orders and were not otherwise relied on); they are the only orders found by a by-number scan (whitespace and hyphenation normalised, which is needed because the held text of EO 12680 prints the number as '119 58') of all 6,652 held FR-original texts apart from EO 13637. They rewrite or extend individual delegations and re-letter the list but delete none, so every clause stays in force, as amended, until the revocation; the amendments are attached as later events on the clauses they change. The relettering by EO 13030 and EO 13091 moved the Section 42 delegation from subsection (n) to (o) and then (p). EO 11992 (May 24, 1977; 42 FR 27195-27196, held official FR scan text) established the Committee on Selection of Federal Judicial Officers, an advisory committee under the Federal Advisory Committee Act. All fourteen operative clauses (Secs. 1-8, subsections separated) are quoted verbatim from the held OCR text. The order set its own end in Sec. 8 (termination on December 31, 1978 unless sooner extended); that end did not occur because EO 12110 (sec. 1-101(i), effective December 31, 1978) continued the Committee until December 31, 1980, and EO 12258 (sec. 1-101(g), effective December 31, 1980) continued it until December 31, 1982, so the chain is unbroken. Before that extended term ran out, EO 12305 of May 5, 1981 (46 FR 25421, item (b)) revoked EO 11992 and terminated the Committee; EO 12305 states no other effective date, so every clause's first end is May 5, 1981, which is also the whole-order end. No amendment of EO 11992 was found (OFR 1989 disposition table: 'Continued by EOs 12110, 12258; Revoked by EO 12305'; USC note at 28 U.S.C. pt. I agrees). The revocation leaves no savings or residual effect.

EO 12305 revokes the whole order and terminates the committee without any savings, transfer or wind-up provision. The order itself creates no property, office tenure or entitlement that could survive: members served without compensation (travel expenses only, payable while engaged in the work), its post-service ineligibility rule is a provision of the revoked order and fell with it, and no function was transferred to another body. No continuing residual found in the order, in EO 12305, or in the later-source searches recorded below.

EO 12064 (June 5, 1978; 43 FR 24661-24662, held official FR scan text) established the United States Tax Court Nominating Commission as a FACA advisory committee. All fifteen numbered operative provisions (1-101 to 1-403) are quoted verbatim. No amendment was found. The order's own end (1-403: December 31, 1978 unless sooner extended) was overtaken by EO 12110 sec. 1-101(l) (effective December 31, 1978, continued to December 31, 1980) and EO 12258 sec. 1-101(j) (effective December 31, 1980, continued to December 31, 1982). EO 12305 of May 5, 1981, item (d), revoked the order and terminated the Commission, effective on signing; every clause therefore first ends on May 5, 1981, the whole-order end. The clause-drafts identity quarantine is resolved: the held page 43 FR 24661 carries the heading 'Executive Order 12064 - June 5,1978, United States Tax Court Nominating Commission'. USC note at 26 U.S.C. 7443 and the OFR 1989 table agree. No savings provision exists.

EO 12305 revokes the whole order and terminates the committee without any savings, transfer or wind-up provision. The order itself creates no property, office tenure or entitlement that could survive: members served without compensation (travel expenses only, payable while engaged in the work), its post-service ineligibility rule is a provision of the revoked order and fell with it, and no function was transferred to another body. No continuing residual found in the order, in EO 12305, or in the later-source searches recorded below.

The dossier carries a single 'whole' clause; because the order has nine distinct provisions I used inventory_overrides to split it into nine disjoint spans (the authority recital is attached to sec. 1-101, and each section heading to the first section under it). EO 13306 pattern conditions tested for this order: (1) ACT records and dossier missing lines: the dossier has no ACT record and no actor text (actor_provisions empty); the three standing missing lines (judgment needed for the current predicate; current-law lead lacks an original-source sha256; no attributed legal-text slice for the current-law pointer) are read and ruled out as bases: the basis of this claim is the held original text, not the lead, and the lead is used only as corroboration. (2) Own-term end: the three machine TERM records are all kind 'report_deadline' and quote the sec. 1-204 recurring six-month report ('The Administrator shall report every six months'); a report deadline is never an end. (3) The dossier has no conflicts. (4) The selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) carry no coverage warning; they cover the U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition through 2026-10-09; laws of 2026-10-10..14 are not reflected, a stated limit), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and the OFR catalog with 17,521 saved order texts (checked 2026-10-19). Corroboration read: the 41 U.S.C. 1701 note in release point 119-121 prints the order's authority recital (the note text held in USC_EO_NOTES.jsonl is truncated after the recital, note id id83c43d4a-3a70-11f1-ab1a-a784e0a454e2), so it corroborates the order's presence in the Code but does not reproduce the sections; eCFR citation leads (20 CFR 654.1, 654.3, 654.8; 44 CFR 331.2) show current regulations implementing it, used as leads only. D6 / later events searched: EDGES.csv has no edge naming EO 12073 as target; a grep of the 6,652 held fr-originals texts (through EO 14435) for 'Executive Order 12073' finds none other than itself; no amendment, revocation, transfer or savings text is known. A reorganization of the named officers (for example the GSA Administrator's functions) would not by itself end a clause and none is found. Limit stated plainly: continuation rests on the original plus the absence of any ending in the bounded searches; whether agencies still perform the program in practice is not asserted, and no attributed current-law slice is held.

EO 12076 (signed 1978-08-18, 43 FR 37161-37162), read in full from the held FR text, places 17 positions in level IV and 14 positions in level V of the Executive Schedule (secs. 1-101, 1-102), preserves the appointments of incumbents (sec. 1-201) and revokes EO 11861, as amended (sec. 1-202). The order has no sunset, termination or report clause. The machine own-term kinds ('condition' and an undated 'fixed_term', plus a quoted conflict) are all noise: they were picked up from other documents printed on the same Federal Register pages (the public-inspection notice, a list of rules going into effect, and a Governors' proclamation), not from the order. EO 12154 (signed 1979-09-04, 44 FR 51965, held FR text, read in full; reading record LSP-EO_12154) sec. 1-202 revokes it 'as amended' with no effective-date wording, so the revocation took effect on signing. Three orders amended EO 12076 before that and were read in full: EO 12099 (1978-11-17) moves the Director of Policy Review, Department of Defense, from level V (item 1-102(e)) to level IV (new item (r)); EO 12111 (1979-01-02) deletes the Interior position in item 1-102(g) and adds a Commerce position as (s); EO 12119 (1979-02-14) deletes the Justice position in item 1-101(f) and inserts a Treasury position. Those three items therefore have an earlier first end than the revocation (1-102(e) on 1978-11-17, 1-102(g) on 1979-01-02, 1-101(f) on 1979-02-14), and the two list leads carry all three amendments as later events; every other clause ends with the revocation. Inventory correction: the dossier's 31 item clauses mis-bound items (q) and (n-dup2) and omit secs. 1-201 and 1-202 (see inventory_overrides, 35 clauses). A by-number scan finds EO 12076 named only in EO 12099, 12111, 12119 and 12154; the dossier conflict (a quarantined Stage 19 relationship) is addressed in conflict_resolutions. Reading record LSP-EO_12154 (EO 12154, 44 FR 51965, read once in full): sec. 1-101 and 1-102 place positions in levels IV and V, sec. 1-201 provides that 'Nothing in this Order shall be deemed to terminate or otherwise affect the appointment, or to require the reappointment, of any occupant of any position listed in Section 1-1 of this Order who was the occupant of that position immediately prior to the issuance of this Order', and sec. 1-202 revokes EO 12076, as amended. EO 12305 revokes the whole order and terminates the committee without any savings, transfer or wind-up provision. EO 12150 (signed July 23, 1979; 44 FR 43455), read in full in the held FR text, has one operative sentence: Section 1(b) of EO 11896 (Jan. 13, 1976, establishing the U.S. Sinai Support Mission; I read its sec. 1 in the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11896.txt) 'is hereby amended to read' a new paragraph (b) that redefines the Mission's duties by reference to the 1975 Basic Agreement 'as superseded by the Treaty of Peace' of March 26, 1979 and Article VII of the Appendix to Annex I. EO 12227 (signed July 22, 1980; 45 FR 49237), read in full from the held actor text, states that 'Sections 1(b) and 1(c) of Executive Order No. 11896 ..., as amended, are hereby further amended to read as follows' and prints an entirely new paragraph (b) (the Mission 'assist[s] in the implementation of the provisions of Annex I and the Appendix to Annex I' of the Treaty by verification tasks). The text inserted by EO 12150 therefore ceased to exist in EO 11896 when EO 12227 took effect; the OFR catalog confirms both as amendments of EO 11896. EO 12227 states no effective date and has no savings or transition clause, so it took effect on signing, 1980-07-22. Later events (EO 12357 of Apr. 6, 1982 adding wind-down sec. 2(g); EO 12553 of Feb. 25, 1986 revoking EO 11896 and its amendments) post-date the first end and are not used. EO 12295 (February 24, 1981; 46 FR 14113, held official FR scan text) has one operative sentence: under section 126a(2) of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 the President, having made the statutory determination and notified Congress, extends the period for continued peaceful nuclear cooperation with EURATOM (already extended by EO 12193) 'to March 10, 1982'. That fixed end date is the order's own term, not a reporting deadline: when it arrived the extension the order granted was used up. EO 12351 of March 9, 1982 gave a new, separate extension to March 10, 1983 (recorded as a later event; it does not amend EO 12295), and the series continued by annual orders. The 1987 revocation by EO 12608 Sec. 1 therefore follows an earlier actual cessation and is recorded as a later formal event. First end of the clause and whole-order end: March 10, 1982, by expiry under the order's own terms. The USC note at 42 U.S.C. 2155 ('extended the period ... to Mar. 10, 1982') and the OFR 1989 table ('Revoked by EO 12608') are consistent with this.

The order's only effect was to keep the statutory cooperation period open until March 10, 1982. Cooperation after that date rests on EO 12351 and later annual extensions (successor authority). Neither EO 12295 nor EO 12608 contains a savings provision for it, and no accrued or continuing effect attributable to EO 12295 was found.

EO 12332 (Nov. 10, 1981; 46 FR 55913) established the National Productivity Advisory Committee under FACA. All twelve operative subsections (secs. 1(a)-4(b)) concern that Committee: composition, advisory functions, agency information, unpaid service, Treasury support, the Executive Secretary, the FACA delegation to the Secretary of the Treasury, and the sec. 4(b) sunset of December 31, 1982 'unless sooner extended'. EO 12399 sec. 1(l), effective December 31, 1982 (sec. 6), continued the Committee 'until September 30, 1984'. The next continuance order, EO 12489 (Sept. 28, 1984), lists other committees but not this one, and no other held order, OFR catalog note or the 1989 Codification ('Continued by EO 12399'; 'Revoked by EO 12534') shows a further extension. The Committee therefore terminated on September 30, 1984, which is the first end of every clause and the whole-order end. EO 12734 (signed 1990-11-14, 55 FR 48099), read in full from the held FR text, is a single paragraph that invokes the emergency construction authority at 10 U.S.C. 2808 in support of the national emergency declared in EO 12722 (Iraq) and takes effect immediately; it has no term, sunset or report deadline. EO 13350 (69 FR 46055, read in full; reading record scale/readings/LSP-EO_13350.json) terminates that emergency and, in its preamble, revokes EO 12722, 12724, 12734, 12743, 12751 and 12817 as based on it; sec. 10 makes it effective at 12:01 a.m. EDT on July 30, 2004, so the first end is 2004-07-30. Dossier leads 'target provision not located: EO:12722' and '... EO:12724' resolved: EO 12722 (55 FR 31803, held FR text) declared the emergency and EO 12724 (55 FR 33089) imposed sanctions; neither mentions EO 12734 or 10 U.S.C. 2808 and both predate it, so both are ruled out as events on this order. EO 13235 (66 FR 58343, 2001) invokes the same statutory authority for the 2001 emergency and does not name EO 12734, so it is ruled out. A by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR-original texts finds EO 12734 named only in EO 13350. The dossier's single 'whole' clause covers the entire operative paragraph. Limit: the annual continuation notices keeping the emergency alive to 2004 are not orders and are not held; EO 13350 itself recites that the emergency was still in force, and no held source records an earlier end. Savings: the S0 prefill is overruled, see savings_residuals.

Reading record LSP-EO_13350 (EO 13350, 69 FR 46055-46057, read once in full; Annex pages are images): sec. 1 provides, under NEA sec. 202(a), that termination of the emergency declared in EO 12722 'shall not affect any action taken or proceeding pending but not finally concluded or determined as of the effective date of this order, any action or proceeding based on any act committed prior to such date, or any rights or duties that matured or penalties that were incurred prior to such date'; the preamble revokes EO 12734 as one of the orders 'based on that national emergency', so the clause reaches it. Own-residual check, reading EO 12734 in full: it invoked 10 U.S.C. 2808 for the Secretary of Defense and the military department Secretaries, so construction projects authorized and funds obligated under that authority before 2004-07-30 are actions taken under the order that the savings clause preserves; the order itself created no new office, right or fund. EO 12852 (signed June 29, 1993; 58 FR 35841-35842), read in full from the held FR text, created the President's Council on Sustainable Development for 2 years (sec. 4(b)). Four later orders amended it: EO 12855 (1993-07-19, administrative support moved to Interior), EO 12965 (1995-06-27, term to June 29, 1997), EO 12980 (1995-11-17, 29 members), EO 13053 (1997-06-30, 35 members, Interior to Energy, term to February 28, 1999) and EO 13114 (1999-02-25, term to June 30, 1999), each read in full from the held FR text.
