It has no term, sunset or termination clause, no report deadline and no condition; the machine own-term list is empty. First end: EO 13345 (69 FR 41901-41903, read in full; reading record readings/LSP-EO_13345.json) sec. 6(c) revokes it ('The following Executive Orders are hereby revoked: ... (c) Executive Order 13028 of December 3, 1996'), whole scope, no exception, no effective-date wording, so effective on signing, 2004-07-08 (machine ACT scope 'whole', class on_signing, confirmed from the text). The parent EO 12757 and the other amending order EO 12823 are revoked in the same sentence (secs. 6(a), 6(b)), so the amended text ends the same day. Dossier leads read: 'target provision not located: EO:12823' - EO 12823 (1992-12-03) is the EARLIER amending order of the same parent; it is not an event on EO 13028 and is itself revoked by EO 13345 sec. 6(b). 'EO:13131' - EO 13131 (1999-07-22) further amends the same parent; attached as a later event on sec1-a and sec1-b (not an end; it strikes none of EO 13028's insertions). Other actor provision ACT:EO:13028>EO:13118: EO 13118 (1999-03-31) amends EO 12163 Part 1-1 (State Department delegations) and names EO 12757 only to exclude the functions that EO 12757 already delegated from the State delegation; it neither amends nor limits EO 13028 and is ruled out. A by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR-original order texts (EO 7532-14435) finds EO 13028 named only in EO 13131 and EO 13345, and EO 12757 named only in EO 12823, 13028, 13118, 13131 and 13345, so no other amendment, extension or reinstatement of the text EO 13028 amended is recorded. Inventory: the dossier's 11 clauses cover the operative text from Sec. 1 through Sec. 2. Inventory correction: the dossier's clauses 'sec1-a' ('(a) The Preamble is amended:') and 'sec1-b' ('(b) Section 1 is amended:') are 28 and 25 characters, too short for the claim-checker's quotation test; inventory_overrides merge each with its sub-items (6 spans, no gap or overlap; every other span unchanged). Reading record readings/LSP-EO_13345.json (EO 13345, 69 FR 41901-41903, read once in full): sec. 6 revokes EO 12757, 12823, 13028 and 13131 in one sentence with no savings, pending-matter, transition or exception clause; sec. 7 only disclaims private rights; sec. 5(b) lets officers 'further assign functions assigned by this order' (EO 13345's own functions, not this order's). The functions EO 13345 designates (sec. 1 Treasury; sec. 2 State) are named by statute: ATDA Act sections 603(b), 604(a), 611, 607 and 614 and Foreign Assistance Act sections 703, 704(a), 805(b), 806(a), 807(a), 808(a), 812 and 813(a). Extension check: no order in the held corpus continues or extends the Committee (a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR-original texts finds EO 13080 named only in EO 13093 and EO 13225, and a name search for 'American Heritage Rivers' finds only EO 13061, 13080, 13093 and 13225), so the Committee's own term ended no later than 2000-04-07. EO 13101 (signed 1998-09-14, 63 FR 49643-49651), read in full from the held FR text, directs executive agencies to prefer recycled and environmentally preferable products and to prevent waste and recycle: it defines terms (Part 2), creates a Steering Committee, a Federal Environmental Executive, a Task Force and Agency Environmental Executives (Part 3), sets acquisition-planning, affirmative-procurement, EPA-designation, paper-content and agency-goal duties with many dated and reporting provisions (Parts 4-6), and adds applicability, recycling-program, training and awards provisions (Parts 7-8) and the revocation of EO 12873 (sec. 901). It has no term, sunset or termination-on-performance clause; every timed provision is a performance, action or reporting deadline, not an end. EO 13423 (signed 2007-01-24) sec. 11(a)(i) revokes it by number, whole order and without qualifier or effective-date wording, so every clause first ends on signing, 2007-01-24. Checked and ruled out as earlier ends or changes: the dossier's 'target provision not located' leads (EO 12843, 12845, 12856, 12902, 12969, 13031, 13134, 13148, 13149) are OFR 'See' cross-references in both directions and operative-text mentions; none amends, extends or revokes EO 13101 (EO 13134 sec. 7(b) borrows its definition of 'biobased product'; EO 13148 secs. 306, 307, 403(b), 503(b), 1001 and 1008 and EO 13149 refer to its sections). The by-number scan of every held FR order text finds EO 13101 named only in EO 13134, 13148, 13149 and 13423 (the other hits are page, document or U.S. Code numbers, for example 42 U.S.C. 13101-13109). EO 13693 sec. 16(a) later revokes EO 13423 with no revival wording, which does not revive EO 13101. The dossier's inventory was corrected: the issuing paragraph was added, mislabelled scopes (sec302-g-2 to -5, sec302-b-dup2, sec402-b/c/d-dup2) were renamed to the sections the text shows, the seven list items of sec. 302(a)(1) were merged into it, sec. 402(d)/403(a) and sec. 901/902 were split where a span held two sections, and page furniture and part headings were cut from the span ends. Limitations: bodies formed under the order (the Steering Committee, Task Force and Agency Environmental Executives) may have had their own charter lives, which no held source records; the claim concerns the order's commands, which the order itself does not end. The dossier's fingerprint changed after selection (a claim-kit rebuild changed only the chain's generic_refs_excluded count 213 to 217) and the new dossier is used; the text is a machine-extracted official PDF text layer, not page images; the cited regulation texts are not held.

rationales.exact_text: Reading record instruments/readings/LSP-EO_13423.json (EO 13423, 72 FR 3919-3923, read once in full): sec. 11(a) revokes EO 13101, 13123, 13134 (as amended), 13148 and 13149 by number with no savings, pending-matter, transition or effective-date wording; sec. 10(a)-(c) are the order's own implementation and no-rights clauses; sec. 11(b) is a stand-alone Department of Defense report through 2010. Own-residual check, reading EO 13101 in full (secs. 101-903): sec. 901 revoked EO 12873 of October 20, 1993 on signing, 1998-09-14, a completed act on another order. EO 13423 revokes EO 13101 without any revival wording, and revoking a revoking order does not by itself revive the order it revoked, so EO 12873 stays revoked: an effect of EO 13101 survives it (accrued). EO 13423 also restates much of EO 13101's machinery as new duties of its own (Steering Committee sec. 4(a), Federal Environmental Executive sec. 6, biobased and recycled-content acquisition and 30 percent post-consumer paper sec. 2(d), waste prevention and recycling programs sec. 2(e)), so the subject was carried forward by a successor order, not left to lapse. The order created no fund, property or private right (sec. 902). The three current-law leads (48 CFR 2823.404-70, 48 CFR 552.238-78, 41 CFR 102-76.55) cite EO 13101; only snippets are held, so no independent regulatory command is established from them. S4 prefill (review, conflict) resolved: the state is transferred_or_accrued because of the completed revocation of EO 12873 and the successor duties; the prefill gave no state. Bounded search: EO 13423 and the order in full; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held Federal Register order texts (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts) for the order's number; OFR catalog edges (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv, which list EO 13423 as the only amending or ending event); the three machine searches; EO 13693 sec. 16(a) (revokes EO 13423, 2015-03-19) read for revival wording (none).

EO 13131 (signed 1999-07-22, 64 FR 40733-40734; 'Further Amendments to Executive Order 12757, Implementation of the Enterprise for the Americas Initiative'), read in full from the held FR text, extends EO 12757 (as amended by EO 12823 and 13028) to the Tropical Forest Conservation Act of 1998: Title, Preamble, Section 1 delegations, Board advice and agreements (Sections 3(b), 3(c)), Board membership (Sections 4(a), 4(c), 4(d)) and a judicial-review clause (Sec. 2). It has no term, sunset or termination clause, no report deadline and no condition; the machine own-term list is empty. First end: EO 13345 (69 FR 41901-41903, read in full; reading record readings/LSP-EO_13345.json) sec. 6(d) revokes it ('The following Executive Orders are hereby revoked: ... (d) Executive Order 13131 of July 22, 1999'), whole scope, no exception, no effective-date wording, so effective on signing, 2004-07-08 (machine ACT scope 'whole', class on_signing, confirmed from the text). The parent EO 12757 and the other amending orders EO 12823 and EO 13028 are revoked in the same sentence, so the amended text ends the same day. Dossier leads read: 'target provision not located: EO:12823' and 'EO:13028' are the two EARLIER amending orders of the same parent (EO 13131 amends the parent 'as amended by Executive Orders 12823 and 13028'); neither amends, extends or limits EO 13131, and both are revoked by EO 13345 sec. 6(b) and 6(c). No other actor provision is listed in the dossier. A by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR-original order texts (EO 7532-14435) finds EO 13131 named only in EO 13345, and EO 12757 named only in EO 12823, 13028, 13118, 13131 and 13345, so no amendment, extension or reinstatement of EO 13131 or of the text it amended is recorded after 1999-07-22 other than the revocation. EO 13118 (1999-03-31) names EO 12757 only to exclude it from a State Department delegation and predates EO 13131. Inventory: the dossier's 22 clauses cover the operative text from Sec. 1 through Sec. 2. Inventory correction: the dossier's parent clauses 'sec1-b' to 'sec1-e' ('(b) The Preamble is amended:', '(c) Section 1 is amended:', '(d) Section 3(b) is amended:', '(e) Section 3(c) is amended:') are 25-28 characters, too short for the claim-checker's quotation test; inventory_overrides merge each with its sub-items (11 spans, no gap or overlap; every other span unchanged). Savings: see savings_residuals (transferred_or_accrued, S1 prefill resolved).

Reading record readings/LSP-EO_13345.json (EO 13345, 69 FR 41901-41903, read once in full): sec. 6 revokes EO 12757, 12823, 13028 and 13131 in one sentence with no savings, pending-matter or exception clause; sec. 5(b) lets officers further assign functions assigned by EO 13345; sec. 1 designates the Secretary of the Treasury, and sec. 2 the Secretary of State, to perform the President's functions under the same statutes EO 13131 had added to EO 12757's delegation. Own-residual check, reading EO 13131 in full: it only amends EO 12757 (Title, Preamble, Sections 1, 3(b), 3(c), 4(a), 4(c)(1), 4(c)(2), 4(d)) and creates no right or fund (sec. 2 disclaims rights). Its substance is carried into EO 13345: the Foreign Assistance Act sections EO 13131 added to the Treasury delegation (805(b), 806(a), 807(a), 808(a), 812) are designated to the Secretary of the Treasury in EO 13345 sec. 1(a)(2), section 813(a) to the Secretary of State in sec. 2(a), the sec. 805(b) determinations 'in accordance with any recommendations' of USAID in sec. 1(b)(1)(B), the Forest Service International Programs and Council on Environmental Quality designees on the Enterprise for the Americas Board (EO 13131 sec. 1(f)) in sec. 4(a)(iii) and (vii), and EO 13131's advice role for the Board on Tropical Forest Agreements is matched by sec. 2(d) and the order's title. The functions and the Board arrangements therefore pass to EO 13345 rather than ending. EO 13147 (2000-03-07), 65 FR 13233 machine text of the Federal Register pages (original_representation_unverified, acceptable_as_original, no page check required). Secs. 1-3(d) establish the White House Commission on Complementary and Alternative Medicine Policy, give it functions (a report to the President), and provide its members' pay, funding and FACA handling; every one is an incident of the Commission. Sec. 3(e): "The Commission shall terminate 2 years from the date of this order unless extended by the President prior to such date." 2000-03-07 plus 2 years = 2002-03-07 (anniversary convention). The condition 'unless extended' was searched: EO 13167 (2000-09-15) changes only sec. 1 membership; EO 13316 (2003-09-17, effective 2003-09-30) revokes the order, with the Commission described as a committee that 'terminated or whose work is completed'; the U.S. Code note at 42 U.S.C. 287c-21 records the same revocation and no extension (editorial lead only). No extension order is held. The 2003 revocation is later than the term date and is not the first end.

EO 13148 (signed 2000-04-21, 65 FR 24595-24606), read in full from the held FR text, makes agency heads responsible for environmental management and sets goals (Part 2: environmental management systems, compliance audits, right-to-know reporting, 40 percent toxic-release and 50 percent use-reduction goals by December 31, 2006, phase-out planning for Class I ozone-depleting substances by 2010), planning and accountability duties (Part 3), management-system, audit, awards, training, compliance-assistance and assurance duties with 4- to 24-month clocks (Part 4), emergency-planning and toxic-chemical reporting and reduction provisions (Part 5), landscaping (Part 6), acquisition and procurement limits (Part 7), national-security exemptions and OMB compliance modification (Part 8), general provisions including the revocation of EO 12843, 12856, 12969, a 1994 memorandum and section 1-4 of EO 12088 (Part 9) and definitions (Part 10). It has no term, sunset or termination-on-performance clause. The dossier's undated 'fixed_term' own-terms (the 'within 12 months after environmentally benign pressure sensitive adhesives ... become commercially available' clock in sec. 702 and the exemption provisions in sec. 801) are conditional action clocks and exemption wording, not ends; December 31, 2006 target dates in secs. 204, 205 and 503(a) passed 24 days before the revocation and are lapsed performance deadlines, not ends. EO 13423 sec. 11(a)(iv) revokes it by number, whole order and without qualifier or effective-date wording, so every clause first ends on signing, 2007-01-24. rationales.exact_text: Reading record instruments/readings/LSP-EO_13423.json (EO 13423, 72 FR 3919-3923, read once in full): sec. 11(a) revokes EO 13101, 13123, 13134 (as amended), 13148 and 13149 by number with no savings, pending-matter, transition or effective-date wording; sec. 10(a)-(c) are the order's own implementation and no-rights clauses; sec. 11(b) is a stand-alone Department of Defense report through 2010. Own-residual check, reading EO 13148 in full (secs. 101-1009): sec. 901 revoked EO 12843, EO 12856, the Executive Memorandum on Environmentally Beneficial Landscaping of April 26, 1994, EO 12969 and section 1-4 'Pollution Control Plan' of EO 12088 on signing, 2000-04-21: completed acts on other instruments, one of them a partial revocation of a surviving order. EO 13423 revokes EO 13148 without revival wording, and revoking a revoking order does not by itself revive what it revoked, so those stay revoked: an effect of EO 13148 survives it (accrued); the U.S. Code note to 42 U.S.C. 4321 still prints EO 12088 as amended by EO 13148 sec. 901. EO 13423 restates the environmental-management subject as new duties of its own (toxic and hazardous chemical and waste reduction sec. 2(e), environmental management systems sec. 3(b), compliance audits sec. 3(c), reporting sec. 3(g)), so the subject was carried forward by a successor order, not left to lapse; the statutory reporting duties the order repeats (EPCRA sec. 313, PPA sec. 6607, sec. 902(c)) rest on those statutes independently. The order created no fund, property or private right (sec. 902(a)). The three current-law leads (42 U.S.C. 4321 note, 33 CFR 148.737, 28 CFR part 61 Appendix E) cite EO 13148; only snippets are held, so no independent regulatory command is established from them. S4 prefill (review, conflict) resolved: transferred_or_accrued. Bounded search: EO 13423 and the order in full; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held Federal Register order texts (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts) for the order's number; OFR catalog edges (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv, which list EO 13423 as the only amending or ending event); the three machine searches; EO 13693 sec. 16(a) (revokes EO 13423, 2015-03-19) read for revival wording (none).

EO 13283 (signed 2003-01-21, 68 FR 3371-3372), read in full from the held FR text, establishes the Office of Global Communications within the White House Office (sec. 1), states its mission and functions (secs. 2-3), provides administrative support (sec. 4), preserves NSC and agency authorities (secs. 5-6) and carries general provisions (sec. 7). The machine own-term kinds are 'temporary_body' (the 'temporary teams of communicators' of sec. 3(c)) and 'condition' (to the extent permitted by law and subject to the availability of appropriations); the temporary teams are a described activity of the Office, not a term of the Office, and neither hit is an end, a sunset or a report deadline. EO 13385 (signed 2005-09-29, 70 FR 57989-57991, held FR text, read in full; reading record LSP-EO_13385) sec. 9 revokes it and sec. 10 makes the order effective September 30, 2005. Dossier lead 'target provision not located: EO:12333' resolved: EO 13283 sec. 3(a) excludes 'special activities as defined in Executive Order 12333 of December 4, 1981' from the Office's assessment; EO 12333 predates EO 13283 and cannot amend or end it, and the pairing is a cross-reference only, so it is ruled out (the machine's 'large actor context' note for EO 12333 is about that order's size, not an action on EO 13283). A by-number scan (whitespace and hyphenation normalised) of all 6,652 held FR-original texts finds EO 13283 named only in EO 13385. Inventory: the dossier's 13 clauses cover secs. 1-7; inventory_overrides merge the 27-character heading clause for sec. 7 with sec. 7(a), leaving 12 clauses with no gap or overlap.

Reading record LSP-EO_13385 (EO 13385, 70 FR 57989-57991, read once in full): sec. 1 continues sixteen advisory committees to 2007-09-30 and sec. 2 reassigns the President's FACA functions for them (neither list nor reassignment reaches the Office of Global Communications); sec. 3 revokes EO 13328 and 13326; sec. 4 supersedes secs. 1-2 of EO 13316; secs. 5-8 amend EO 13231, 12367, 12216 and 13226; sec. 9 revokes EO 13283 with no qualifier, savings, pending-matter or transition clause; sec. 10 makes the order effective 2005-09-30. The only 'transfer' wording in the order (the sec. 2 FACA reassignment, the S1 prefill's source) is limited to the sec. 1 committees. Own-residual check, reading EO 13283 in full: it created a White House Office element, described its mission and functions, and provided for administrative support; it conferred no right or benefit (sec. 7(a)), granted no authority over agencies (sec. 7(b)), left existing agency authorities unchanged (sec. 6) and transferred no function, fund or property. The S1 prefill ('review') is resolved as none_after_bounded_search. The exact retained official Federal Register page was visually compared to its complete text and signature; its byte hash matches both stage21 custody and full_run source metadata. The current U.S.Code note reproduces the same five clauses, corroborating continuation throughOctober9 rather than supplying a new source of authority. To assess the October14cutoff, the researcher reviewed the saved OFR catalog current to that cutoff, all numeric13306hits and unparsed-note hits, and the bounded eCFR and later-order-text scan described below. Two other catalog numericmatches are page/document-number collisions; no adverse disposition or amendment is identified for this order. This supports continued operation of the original authority within those bounded searches. No judicial or statutory contrarylead is identified in the saved inputs; unnamed statutory displacement and uncatalogued decisions are limitations of the bounded search, not invented findings of absence. No human certification or GPOpublished fixity confirmation is asserted.

No ending,transfer,suspension or independent savings provision appears in the complete original or identified later-source leads. EO 13369 (2005-01-07), 70 FR 2323 machine text (original_representation_unverified, acceptable_as_original). Sec. 1 establishes the President's Advisory Panel on Federal Tax Reform; secs. 2-6 staff and direct it; sec. 7 as issued: "The Advisory Panel shall terminate 30 days after submitting its report pursuant to section 5". EO 13386 (2005-09-30), 70 FR 58289, sec. 2 amended sec. 7 by deleting that phrase and inserting "November 15, 2005". The end is the stated date 2005-11-15, cited to the held text of EO 13386; the report deadlines (July 31, Sept. 30, Nov. 1, 2005) are deadlines and are not used as dates. EO 13380 (dossier gap "target provision not located: EO:13380") is a misparsed OFR note: it amends EO 12916 and was read directly. EO 13446 (2007-09-28, effective 2007-09-30) revokes the order after the end. Producer record OTE:EO:13369@lamm.

Sec. 6(a),(b) are rules of construction with no independent operation once the Panel ends. No clause survives the Panel."}

Read the whole order: no savings, transfer or continuing-effect clause. Sec. 6(a) (nothing impairs OMB functions) and 6(b) (no right or benefit) are rules of construction that attach to the order while it operates; no pending matter, appropriation or function is saved or transferred when the Panel ends. EO 13446 (2007) revoked the order as a completed committee with no savings text.

EO 13771 (signed 2017-01-30, 82 FR 9339; read in full from the held Federal Register text, 19 clauses) states the policy of prudent regulatory costs (sec. 1), imposes a two-for-one offset and a cap for fiscal year 2017 (sec. 2), requires annual regulatory cost submissions and allowances from fiscal year 2018 on (sec. 3), defines regulation (sec. 4) and has general provisions (sec. 5). First ends: eighteen clauses end with the order on 2021-01-20 by EO 13992 sec. 2 (LSP-EO_13992); sec. 2(b) is the exception: it is a cap 'for fiscal year 2017' and stopped operating by its own terms when fiscal year 2017 ended on 2017-09-30, so its first end is that earlier own-terms date (cited to the clause's own text; the fiscal-year end is general law, not a held source). The sec. 2 heading 'Regulatory Cap for Fiscal Year 2017' was weighed against paragraphs (a), (c) and (d), which carry no period and are read as running to the revocation; this is the main judgement call in the claim. The whole-order end is the latest first end, 2021-01-20. Other-actor leads: ACT:EO:13771>EO:13777 and >EO:13783 are false positives (EO 13777 sec. 2(a)(i) lists EO 13771 among the initiatives agency officers oversee, and EO 13783 sec. 2(g) asks agencies to coordinate with it; neither revokes, amends or suspends any part of EO 13771). Dossier missing lines 'target provision not located: EO:12866, 13782, 13790, 13817, 13891': EO 12866 predates it; EO 13782 does not name it; EO 13790 (sec. on the task force coordinating with reviews under it), EO 13817 (implement consistently with it) and EO 13891 (lists it as a compliance standard) only refer to it. Later events on the acting order, tested under D6: EO 14148 sec. 2(g) and EO 14154 (both signed 2025-01-20, held official texts) revoke EO 13992 itself; neither contains reinstatement or revival wording for any order revoked by EO 13992 (searched for 'reinstat' in the held texts of EO 14148, 14154 and 14192; the only hits are in EO 14192 sec. 6(b)-(c), which reinstate OMB Circular A-4 (2003 version) and a Treasury-OMB memorandum of agreement), and EO 14192 sec. 3 sets a new regulatory cap for fiscal year 2025 under its own authority without naming this order. Revoking a revoking order is not a reinstatement, so the 2021-01-20 revocation of this order stands. The U.S. Code note confirms the ending: the machine current-law search found the OLRC note at 5 U.S.C. 601 note that EO 13771 'was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 13992, § 2, Jan. 20, 2021, 86 F.R. 7049'. The three dossier machine searches were read and copied. Own by-number scan (hyphenation and whitespace normalised) of the 6,652 held Federal Register text files in jobs/fr-originals for the bare number 13771 near 'order' or 'Executive Order': EO 13771 is named only in EO 13777, 13783, 13790, 13817, 13891 and 13992 (other hits are page numbers in neighbouring documents). Conflict, savings and the own-residual check are in conflict_resolutions and savings_residuals.

Reading record LSP-EO_13992: sec. 2 revokes EO 13771 whole with no effective-date wording (2021-01-20); sec. 3 directs OMB and agency heads to rescind implementing orders, rules, regulations, guidelines and policies and abolish entities established under the revoked orders; sec. 4(a) is a non-impairment clause for statutory authority and OMB budget functions; nothing is transferred and no exception names EO 13771. Own-residual check, reading EO 13771 in full (secs. 1-5): it created no entity, office, fund, property or right (sec. 5(c)); it set a two-for-one offset and a fiscal year 2017 cap on agencies, an annual regulatory cost allowance process run by OMB (sec. 3) and OMB guidance (secs. 2(d), 3(e)). Regulations that agencies repealed or issued under the offset are agency acts that do not depend on the order, and the order required no agency rule, so nothing of the order itself outlives the revocation; the later EO 14192 (2025-01-31) creates a new regulatory cap for fiscal year 2025 under its own authority and does not name EO 13771, so it is a new instrument and not a continuation. Kept as none_after_bounded_search. EO 13772 (signed February 3, 2017, 82 FR 9965-9966), read in full from the held official FR text, states the Core Principles for regulating the financial system as policy (sec. 1), directs the Treasury Secretary to report to the President within 120 days and periodically thereafter (sec. 2) and has general provisions (sec. 3). It has no term or sunset: the only timing words are the 120-day report deadline, which is a report deadline and never an end. EO 13783 (signed 2017-03-28, 82 FR 16093-16097; 'Promoting Energy Independence and Economic Growth'), read in full from the held FR text, sets the policy (sec. 1), orders agency review of regulations that burden domestic energy (sec. 2: 45-day plans, 120-day draft reports, 180-day final reports), revokes EO 13653, three Presidential memoranda and two reports and orders CEQ guidance rescinded (sec. 3), orders EPA review of the Clean Power Plan and related rules (sec. 4), disbands the social-cost-of-greenhouse-gases working group and withdraws its documents (sec. 5), directs Interior on the coal leasing moratorium (sec. 6), orders EPA and Interior reviews of oil and gas rules (sec. 7) and has general provisions (sec. 8). Own terms: the machine own-term kinds are report_deadline (sec. 2(d), 2(e)), condition (sec. 2(e), 7(b)(iv), 8(b)) and until_event (sec. 7(c)); all are deadlines or conditions on performance, none is an end, and the order has no sunset, duration or termination clause. A report deadline is never an end and no clause's first end needs a report date, so the order is not blocked. First end: EO 13990 (86 FR 7037-7043, read in full; reading record readings/LSP-EO_13990.json) sec. 7(a) revokes it ('are hereby revoked') in the same sentence as EO 13766, 13778, 13792, 13795, 13868 and 13927; the sec. 7(a) exception ('except for sections 6, 7, and 11') belongs to EO 13834 only. EO 13990 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation took effect on signing, 2021-01-20. Machine ACT scope 'whole', effective class on_signing, confirmed from the text. Dossier leads read and ruled out: 'target provision not located: EO:13790' (EO 13790, 82 FR 20237, sec. 4(c) only tells the new Agriculture task force to 'coordinate its efforts with other reviews ... conducted pursuant to' EO 13771, 13778 and 13783: a cross-reference, no amendment or extension) and 'EO:13817' (82 FR 60835, sec. 4(b) tells agencies to implement the critical-minerals strategy 'in a manner consistent with, and when possible complementary to' EO 13783 and others: a cross-reference). A by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR-original order texts (EO 7532 through EO 14435; hyphenation and whitespace normalised) finds EO 13783 named only in EO 13790, EO 13817 and EO 13990, so no amendment, extension, suspension or reinstatement is recorded before or after the revocation. EO 14148 and EO 14154 (2025) revoke EO 13990 but name no order of this batch and reinstate nothing, and the revocation of a revoking order does not revive the order it revoked. Dossier conflict NO_ORDER_CITED_IN_CURRENT_LAW (a DOE regulation cites the order) resolved in conflict_resolutions. Inventory: the dossier's 51 clauses cover the operative text from Sec. 1 through Sec. 8(c); the unnumbered issuing words are not an operative clause. Inventory correction: the dossier labels the two reports in Sec. 3(b) 'sec3-i-dup2' and 'sec3-i-ii-dup2' and omits the lettered parent from other sub-items; inventory_overrides keep every dossier span unchanged and only rename the scopes (51 spans, no gap or overlap). Some dossier spans carry the FR running header or the VerDate footer from a page break; they are left as the dossier has them. Savings: see savings_residuals (continuing_independent, S4 prefill resolved).

rationales.exact_text: Reading record readings/LSP-EO_13990.json (EO 13990, 86 FR 7037-7043, read once in full) and its batch-07 addendum: sec. 7(a) revokes EO 13783 by number in one sentence with no savings, pending-matter or transition clause; the only exception in sec. 7(a) is EO 13834 and the sec. 7(a) list otherwise excepts nothing; sec. 8(a) is a general non-impairment clause for statutory agency authority and OMB functions and saves no revoked order or act; sec. 7(f) tells the OMB Director and agency heads to rescind issuances implementing or enforcing the revoked orders; nothing is transferred. Own-residual check, reading EO 13783 in full: it creates no right, benefit, property or fund (sec. 8(c) disclaims rights) and no continuing body. But parts of it are completed, self-executing acts on OTHER instruments: sec. 3(a) revokes EO 13653 and the Presidential Memoranda of June 25, 2013, November 3, 2015 and September 21, 2016; sec. 3(b) rescinds two Executive Office reports; sec. 5(b) disbands the Interagency Working Group on the Social Cost of Greenhouse Gases and withdraws six of its technical documents. Revoking EO 13783 does not by itself restore any of them. EO 13990 reinstates only EO 13754 and the December 20, 2016 memorandum (sec. 4(b)), and sec. 5(b) establishes a new Working Group without reviving the old documents; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts finds EO 13653 named only in EO 13677, 13683, 13693 and 13783, and no held order reinstates it or the memoranda. Those acts therefore continue independently of EO 13783. S4 prefill ('review', dossier conflict) resolved after reading: state continuing_independent (not none_after_bounded_search). Bounded search: EO 13783, EO 13790, EO 13817 and EO 13990 in full; a by-number scan of all held FR-original texts (EO 7532-14435); U.S. Code and eCFR leads in the dossier. The present legal status of the memoranda and reports themselves is not searched here.

(e) Within 120 days of the date of this order, the Secretary shall provide 
a final report to the President, through the Director of the Office of Manage-
ment and Budget, the Assistant to the President for Economic Policy, the 
Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy, and the Chairman of the 
Council on Environmental Quality, summarizing the findings of the review 
described in subsection (a) of this section. The final report shall include 
recommendations for such Presidential actions, legislative proposals, or other 
actions consistent with law as the Secretary may consider appropriate to 
carry out the policy set forth in section 1 of this order.

EO 13792 (signed 2017-04-26, 82 FR 20429-20431), read in full from the held FR text, orders the Secretary of the Interior to review Antiquities Act monument designations made since 1996 (sec. 2(a)-(c)) and report to the President, an interim report within 45 days and a final report within 120 days (sec. 2(d)-(e)). The machine own-term kinds are report_deadline (sec. 2(d), 2(e)) and condition (sec. 3(b)). A report deadline is never an end; the order has no sunset or termination wording, so every clause remains part of the order until revoked. No clause's first end needs a report date, so the order is not blocked on the report-deadline question; the producer does not claim when either report was delivered. EO 13990 (86 FR 7037-7043, read in full; reading record scale/readings/LSP-EO_13990.json) sec. 7(a) revokes it, effective on signing, 2021-01-20. The dossier lists no missing provision and no other actor provision; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR-original texts finds EO 13792 named only in EO 13990. The monument-boundary proclamations of 2017 were separate Presidential acts, not part of this order. EO 14148 and EO 14154 (2025) revoke EO 13990 but name none of the six orders and reinstate nothing. Inventory: the dossier's 18 clauses cover the operative text from sec. 1 through sec. 3(c); its scope labels for sec. 2(a)(v)-(vii) ('sec2-v', 'sec2-v-vi', 'sec2-v-vii') are irregular but each span is correct and no text is missing or duplicated.

shared_rationale_references.resolved_text: EO 13792 (Review of Designations Under the Antiquities Act, signed 2017-04-26, 82 FR 20429-20431) was read in full from the held official Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13792.txt, OCR text layer of three PDF pages; page images were not inspected and requires_page_check is false). Operative content: Sec. 1 policy; Sec. 2(a)-(c) Secretary of the Interior review of monument designations, factors and consultation; Sec. 2(d)-(e) interim report in 45 days and final report in 120 days (report deadlines, never ends); Sec. 3 general provisions. It has no sunset and no own-terms ending. The first and only end found is Sec. 7(a) of EO 13990 (signed 2021-01-20, 86 FR 7037; held official text, Sec. 7 and Sec. 8 read in full): 'Executive Order 13792 of April 26, 2017 (Review of Designations Under the Antiquities Act) ... are hereby revoked.' The revocation of EO 13792 is unconditional (the exception wording in Sec. 7 concerns only EO 13834, EO 13920 and memoranda) and EO 13990 states no delayed effective date, so it took effect on signing, 2021-01-20. The three machine searches (U.S. Code release 119-121 and eCFR as of 2026-10-14: 0 hits; OFR catalog: 2 hits, both EO 13990, no reinstatement candidate) were read and carry no coverage warning; they show no earlier ending and no later revival. Judgment on performance: the Secretary's review and reports ordered by Sec. 2 may have been completed in 2017, but no held source dates them, a report deadline is not an end and the order is not self-terminating, so the order is treated as operative until revoked on 2021-01-20. The independent reviewer should test that judgment.

EO 13795 (signed 2017-04-28, 82 FR 20815-20818), read in full from the held FR text, sets an offshore energy strategy: lease-sale scheduling and seismic permitting (sec. 3), a sanctuary and marine-monument designation review with a 180-day report (sec. 4(a)-(b)), the revocation of EO 13754 (sec. 4(c)), a modification of three OCS withdrawal memoranda (sec. 5), several rule and guidance reviews (secs. 6-11) and general provisions. The only own-term hits are the implementation condition (sec. 13(b)) and the 60- and 180-day periods, which are deadlines, not ends. EO 13990 (86 FR 7037-7043, read in full; reading record scale/readings/LSP-EO_13990.json) sec. 7(a) revokes it, effective on signing, 2021-01-20. EO 13990 sec. 4(b), the same day, reinstates EO 13754 and the December 20, 2016 memorandum 'in their original form' (86 FR 7039; the U.S. Code notes to 15 U.S.C. 4101 and 43 U.S.C. 1331 record the reinstatement and the revocation). No later amendment of EO 13795 before the revocation appears in the held FR texts (by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR-original texts: only EO 13990 names it), the OFR catalog edges or the U.S. Code notes. EO 14148 and EO 14154 (2025) revoke EO 13990 but name none of the six orders and reinstate nothing. Inventory: the dossier's 24 clauses cover the operative text from sec. 1 through sec. 13(c). Savings: the S0 prefill is overruled, see savings_residuals.

Reading record scale/readings/LSP-EO_13990.json (EO 13990, 86 FR 7037-7043, read once in full): sec. 7(a) revokes EO 13795 with no savings clause; sec. 8(a) saves only statutory agency authority; sec. 7(f) tells the OMB Director and agency heads to rescind issuances implementing or enforcing the revoked orders; sec. 4(b) reinstates EO 13754 and the December 20, 2016 memorandum 'in their original form' and names no other memorandum. Own-residual check, reading EO 13795 in full: sec. 5 is self-executing. It modifies 'to read, in its entirety' the body text of three OCS withdrawal memoranda (December 20, 2016; January 27, 2015; July 14, 2008), withdrawing the sanctuary areas 'for a time period without specific expiration', and adds that 'nothing in the withdrawal under this section affects any rights under existing leases'. A modification already made to other Presidential instruments, and a lease-rights proviso, do not lapse when the modifying order is revoked. EO 13990 sec. 4(b) undoes the change only for the December 20, 2016 memorandum (and EO 13754, revoked by sec. 4(c)); it does not mention the January 27, 2015 or July 14, 2008 memoranda, so by its terms their text as modified stays. S0 prefill (none_after_bounded_search) OVERRULED: the prefill finds no savings wording because EO 13990 has none, but the order's own sec. 5 effect continues under the memoranda themselves (OCSLA sec. 12(a)). Bounded search: EO 13795, EO 13990 in full; a by-number scan of all held FR-original texts (EO 13754 appears only in EO 13795 and EO 13990); U.S. Code notes to 15 U.S.C. 4101 and 43 U.S.C. 1331. The status of the 2015 and 2008 memoranda today is not searched here.

EO 13807 (signed 2017-08-15, 82 FR 40463-40469; 'Establishing Discipline and Accountability in the Environmental Review and Permitting Process for Infrastructure Projects'), read in full from the held FR text, sets the purpose and policy (secs. 1-2), definitions (sec. 3), a Cross-Agency Priority Goal and performance accountability system (sec. 4), process enhancements - 'One Federal Decision', permitting timetables, the Dashboard, EO 13766 implementation, CEQ and FPISC duties, energy corridors and an Interior reorganization strategy (sec. 5) - the revocation of EO 13690 (sec. 6) and general provisions (sec. 7). Own terms: the machine own-term kinds are condition (sec. 5(b)(ii)-(iii), 5(c), 5(d), 5(f)(i), 7(b)), fixed_term (sec. 4(b)) and until_event (sec. 5(b)(iv)). The fixed_term is the '180 days of the establishment of the CAP Goal, or such longer period as determined by the Director of OMB' for OMB's accountability guidance: a deadline for performing a command, not an end. The until_event is 'until the design of a project has sufficiently advanced': a rule about when a project's timetable dates may be left blank, not an end. The order has no sunset, duration or termination clause. No clause's first end needs a report date, so the order is not blocked. First end: EO 13990 (86 FR 7037-7043, read in full; reading record readings/LSP-EO_13990.json) sec. 7(b) says 'Executive Order 13807 ... is hereby revoked'; whole scope, no exception (the only sec. 7 exception is EO 13834); no effective-date wording, so effective on signing, 2021-01-20. Machine ACT scope 'whole', effective class on_signing, confirmed from the text. Dossier leads read and ruled out as ends or amendments: 'target provision not located: EO:13766' (EO 13807 sec. 5(d) implements EO 13766 and redirects the CEQ Chairman's secs. 2-3 responsibilities; EO 13766 was revoked by EO 13990 sec. 7(a) the same day: nothing earlier); 'EO:13781' (sec. 5(h) tells OMB to fold Interior's strategy into the plan under EO 13781: a coordination cross-reference); 'EO:13817' (sec. 4(b) of EO 13817 tells agencies to implement the critical-minerals strategy consistently with EO 13807: a cross-reference). Other actor provision ACT:EO:13807>EO:14030: EO 14030 sec. 5(e) does not revoke EO 13807 (it narrates that EO 13807 had revoked EO 13690 and reinstates EO 13690); it is attached as a later event on sec6 only. EO 13921 sec. 6(a) (2020-05-07; effective on signing, no effective-date wording) tells agencies reviewing aquaculture projects to 'use the ''One Federal Decision'' process enhancements described in section 5(b) of Executive Order 13807': an incorporation by reference of sec. 5(b), not an amendment, suspension or revocation of EO 13807, so no later event is attached (EO 13921 is also not among the dossier's evidence records, so it could not be attached); EO 14276 (2025-04-17, 90 FR 16993) says EO 13921 'remains in effect', and the use of the process for aquaculture continues under EO 13921 itself after EO 13807's revocation - see savings_residuals. A by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR-original order texts finds EO 13807 named only in EO 13817, 13921, 13990 and 14030, so no amendment, extension, suspension or reinstatement of EO 13807 itself is recorded. EO 14148 and EO 14154 (2025) revoke EO 13990 but do not name EO 13807 or reinstate it, and the revocation of a revoking order does not revive the order it revoked. rationales.exact_text: Reading record readings/LSP-EO_13990.json (EO 13990, 86 FR 7037-7043, read once in full) and its batch-07 addendum: sec. 7(b) revokes EO 13807 by number with no savings, pending-matter or transition clause; sec. 8(a) is a general non-impairment clause for statutory agency authority and OMB functions and saves no revoked order; sec. 7(f) tells the OMB Director and agency heads to rescind issuances implementing or enforcing the revoked orders; sec. 7(b)'s second sentence only tells the OMB Director and CEQ Chair to 'consider whether to recommend that a replacement order be issued' (a direction to consider, not a transfer). Own-residual check, reading EO 13807 in full: it creates no right, benefit, property or fund (sec. 7(c) disclaims rights) and no body. Three things need a state. (1) Sec. 6 is a completed act on another instrument: it revoked EO 13690 (Federal Flood Risk Management Standard). EO 13990 did not reinstate EO 13690, so that revocation outlived EO 13807 until EO 14030 sec. 5(e) expressly reinstated EO 13690 on 2021-05-20 (attached as a later event on sec6). (2) Sec. 5(b)'s 'One Federal Decision' process is incorporated by reference in EO 13921 sec. 6(a), which EO 14276 (2025) says remains in effect; the process continues to be directed for aquaculture projects independently of EO 13807 (recorded here; not attachable as a later event because it neither amends, suspends nor revokes the clause and EO 13921 is not among the dossier's evidence records). (3) Functions it assigned or re-delegated (sec. 5(d) CEQ-to-FPISC referrals for EO 13766, sec. 5(f) GSA support and delegations, sec. 5(h) Interior strategy) lapse with the order or rest on 42 U.S.C. 4370m-4370m-12 and the agencies' own authority; EO 13990 sec. 8(a) saves only that statutory authority and moves nothing. S1 prefill ('review', transfer wording) resolved after reading: state continuing_independent (not transferred_or_accrued and not none_after_bounded_search). Bounded search: EO 13807, EO 13766, EO 13817, EO 13921, EO 13990, EO 14030 and EO 14276 in full or in the cited sections; a by-number scan of all held FR-original texts (EO 7532-14435). The present status of the Framework Memorandum of March 20, 2018 and of EO 13690 after the 2025 revocation of EO 14030 are outside this order's lifecycle and not searched.

EO 13828 (signed April 10, 2018, 83 FR 15941-15944), read in full from the held official FR text, states the Principles of Economic Mobility as policy (sec. 2), directs eight Secretaries to review regulations and programs, report within 90 days and take steps to implement recommended administrative actions (sec. 3), defines terms (sec. 4) and has general provisions (sec. 5). It has no term or sunset: the only timing words are the 90-day review and report deadlines in sec. 3, which are deadlines and never ends. EO 14018 sec. 1 (reading record LSP-EO_14018, read once in full) revokes the order with no effective-date wording, effective on signing 2021-02-24. The dossier's ACT record is built on the held official FR text of EO 14018 and carries the sec. 1 sentence naming the order; its scope is whole. The dossier lists no missing provision and no conflict. The dossier's 40 clauses run contiguously from the first section to the signature line, so the inventory is kept as is. D6 (any later event that ended or changed a clause): a by-number scan of all 6,652 held official FR order texts finds EO 13828 named only in EO 14018 (EO 9805 holds 13828 as a CFR page number); the OFR catalog edges (4 rows) and the USC note at 5 U.S.C. 601 note record only the EO 14018 revocation; no amendment, extension or reinstatement appears in those sources. Savings: none_after_bounded_search, see savings_residuals.

Reading record LSP-EO_14018 (EO 14018, 86 FR 11855-11856, read once in full): sec. 1 revokes five Executive orders and two memoranda with no effective-date wording; sec. 2 treats rules and policies implementing a listed order as separate acts for the agencies to consider rescinding and abolishes entities created under the listed actions as appropriate and consistent with law; sec. 3(a) is a no-impair clause for statutory agency authority and OMB functions only; there is no successor delegation, transfer of functions or funds, pending-matter clause or exception. The two transfer-wording hits the machine counted are words in the title of a revoked Memorandum ('Delegation of Certain Authority Under the Federal Service Labor-Management Relations Statute'), not an operative transfer. Own-residual check, reading EO 13828 in full (secs. 1-5): it states the Principles of Economic Mobility as policy, directs the review, report and implementation steps and defines terms; it created no office, fund or right, transferred no function and revoked or amended no earlier order. Administrative actions an agency took under sec. 3 are that agency's own acts under its statutes, which EO 14018 sec. 2 treats as separate acts to consider rescinding; sec. 5(c) disclaims private rights. EO 13834 (signed 2018-05-17, 83 FR 23771-23774), read in full from the held FR text, sets efficient-operations goals for agencies (secs. 1-2), implementation actions with 45- to 150-day periods (sec. 3), duties of the CEQ Chairman including the continuation of the Steering Committee (sec. 4), of the OMB Director (sec. 5), of the Federal Chief Sustainability Officer (sec. 6) and of agency heads (sec. 7), the revocation of EO 13693 (sec. 8) and limitations, exemptions and general provisions (secs. 9-11). The machine own-term kind is condition only (sec. 11(b)). The order has no sunset or termination clause. Two later orders end it in two steps, which is why its clauses have two different first ends. EO 13990 (signed 2021-01-20, 86 FR 7037-7043, held FR text, read in full; reading record scale/readings/LSP-EO_13990) sec. 7(a) says EO 13834 'is hereby revoked except for sections 6, 7, and 11', with no effective-date wording, so sections 1-5 and 8-10 ended on 2021-01-20; the dossier's machine ACT scope 'partial' for this record is correct, and its ACT record 'ACT:EO:13834>EO:13990' (the official FR text, split across the printed pages 7041-7042) is the first end for those clauses. EO 14057 (signed 2021-12-08, 86 FR 70935-70943, held FR text, read in full; reading record LSP-EO_14057) sec. 604 revokes EO 13834 in full, with no effective-date wording, so sections 6, 7 and 11 ended on 2021-12-08; the dossier's end ACT record for EO 14057 quotes the American Presidency Project transcription, so that end is cited by ACTOR_TEXT:EO:14057 (the official FR text). The batch scout's single end date (EO 14057, whole) would have misdated 28 of the 40 clauses, which is the earlier-partial-supersession lesson of Lambertini II (as with EO 10746 via EO 10900). A by-number scan (whitespace and hyphenation normalised) of all 6,652 held FR-original texts finds EO 13834 named only in EO 13990 and EO 14057. EO 14148 (2025-01-20) later revoked EO 13990 but does not name EO 13834 and reinstates nothing, and EO 13834 had been revoked in full by EO 14057 more than three years earlier, so the 2025 revocation of EO 13990 revives no part of it. Inventory: the dossier's 41 clauses cover secs. 1-11 from the Policy section through sec. 11(c); inventory_overrides merge the one fragment 'sec6-4375' into sec. 6, leaving 40 clauses with no gap or overlap. Several clauses cross a page break and so contain the running head of the next page, as the dossier segmented them.

Reading record LSP-EO_14057 (EO 14057, 86 FR 70935-70943, read once in full): sec. 501 'reestablishe[s]' the Office of the Federal Chief Sustainability Officer within CEQ, sec. 502 has agencies designate Chief Sustainability Officers and secs. 504-508 reset the CEQ, OMB and agency duties and create working groups; sec. 604 revokes EO 13834 with no savings, transition or exception clause; the order mentions neither the Steering Committee nor any surviving provision of EO 13834, and its sec. 606(a) is a general non-impairment clause for agency authority. Reading record LSP-EO_13990 (reused, 86 FR 7037-7043): sec. 7(a) revoked EO 13834 on 2021-01-20 except secs. 6, 7 and 11; sec. 7(f) directs rescission of implementing measures. Own-residual check, reading EO 13834 in full: the one savings lead (the S3 prefill) is sec. 4(a), under which the Federal Interagency Sustainability Steering Committee 'shall continue in effect'; sec. 4 was among the sections revoked by EO 13990 on 2021-01-20, the Committee was a body continued by this order and not created by it, and EO 14057 does not mention it, so no continuing provision survives the revocation of the order. Sec. 6 (the Federal Chief Sustainability Officer and the Office of Federal Sustainability) is replaced by the re-established Office in EO 14057 sec. 501, which re-creates rather than preserves; sec. 8 revoked EO 13693, an executed revocation that nothing revives; the order created no right (sec. 11(c) disclaims rights), fund or property. The S3 prefill ('review') is therefore overruled to none_after_bounded_search for the reasons given. EO 13875 (signed 2019-06-14, 84 FR 28711; read in full from the held Federal Register text) orders agencies to evaluate and terminate FACA advisory committees (sec. 1), caps eligible committees at 350 (sec. 2), sets reporting requirements (sec. 3), assigns OMB a role including waivers and recommendations (sec. 4), exempts merit review panels (sec. 5) and carries general provisions (sec. 6). Own-terms leads: the dossier's undated 'sunset_date' terms are the sec. 1(b) deadline 'by September 30, 2019' and the sec. 1(e) look-back; both are read in the clause reasons as performance deadlines and a counting window, not as ends of the order or of any clause, and its report_deadline terms (Aug. 1 and Sept. 1, 2019) are never ends. The limit of this reading: a command already performed may have been exhausted before 2021-01-20, which no held source dates, so the project rule 'a deadline is not an end' is followed and the revocation date is the first end of each clause. No amendment, suspension or extension of EO 13875 is found: the dossier lists no other-actor provision and no missing line, and the by-number scan finds EO 13875 named only in EO 13992 sec. 2. EO 13992 sec. 2 revokes it on signing, 2021-01-20 (LSP-EO_13992). Later events on the acting order, tested under D6: EO 14148 sec. 2(g) and EO 14154 (both signed 2025-01-20, held official texts) revoke EO 13992 itself; neither contains reinstatement or revival wording for any order revoked by EO 13992 (searched for 'reinstat' in the held texts of EO 14148, 14154 and 14192; the only hits are in EO 14192 sec. 6(b)-(c), which reinstate OMB Circular A-4 (2003 version) and a Treasury-OMB memorandum of agreement), and EO 14192 sec. 3 sets a new regulatory cap for fiscal year 2025 under its own authority without naming this order. Revoking a revoking order is not a reinstatement, so the 2021-01-20 revocation of this order stands. The machine current-law searches found no hit for this order (no OLRC or eCFR mention); the OFR catalog edges are the revocation. Own by-number scan (hyphenation and whitespace normalised) of the 6,652 held Federal Register text files in jobs/fr-originals for the bare number 13875 near 'order' or 'Executive Order': EO 13875 is named only in EO 13992 sec. 2. Savings and the own-residual check are in savings_residuals.

Reading record LSP-EO_13992: sec. 2 revokes EO 13875 whole with no effective-date wording (2021-01-20); sec. 3 directs OMB and agencies to rescind implementing orders, rules and policies and abolish entities established under the revoked orders 'as appropriate and consistent with applicable law'; sec. 4(a) is a non-impairment clause for statutory authority and OMB budget functions; nothing is transferred and no exception names EO 13875. Own-residual check, reading EO 13875 in full (secs. 1-6): it established no committee, office, fund or right; it required agencies to review and terminate FACA committees, cap the total at 350, report to OMB and let OMB recommend terminations. Committees an agency terminated under sec. 1(b) stay terminated, but each termination is an agency act under FACA authority and not an effect of the order that outlives it; EO 13992 sec. 3 has no entity of EO 13875 to abolish. The order has no implementing rule requirement. The prefill was S1 (transfer wording): the 'transfer' phrases belong to EO 13992 sec. 3 (rescission and abolition), which transfers nothing; kept as none_after_bounded_search after reading both orders. Bounded search: EO 13875 and EO 13992 in full; current-law usc/ecfr searches (no hit); the by-number scan.

EO 13891 (signed 2019-10-09, 84 FR 55235; read in full from the held Federal Register text, 38 clauses) sets the policy that guidance documents be non-binding (sec. 1), defines terms (sec. 2), requires agencies to publish a database of guidance documents and rescind unneeded ones (sec. 3), to finalize regulations on guidance-document procedures (sec. 4), applies EO 12866, 13563 and 13609 to guidance (sec. 5), tells OMB to implement (sec. 6) and has general provisions and carve-outs (sec. 7). Own-terms: the dossier flags 'fixed_term' leads (the '240 days' reinstatement window in sec. 3(b) and 'at least 30 days' of public comment in sec. 4(a)(iii)(A)), a 'report_deadline' (sec. 3(d)) and conditions. Read in the clause reasons: the 120/240/300-day periods run from the date of an OMB implementing memorandum that no held source dates, they are performance and reporting deadlines, the 240-day reinstatement permission narrows sec. 3(b) without ending it, and the 30-day period is a minimum comment requirement; none is an end of a clause or the order. EO 13992 sec. 2 revokes it on signing, 2021-01-20 (LSP-EO_13992). Dossier missing lines 'target provision not located: EO:12866, 13563, 13771, 13777, 1609': these orders predate EO 13891 (1993, 2011, 2017, 2017) and cannot amend it, and 'EO 1609 of May 1, 2012' in the OFR cross-reference is the mistyped number of EO 13609 (2012); EO 13891 only lists them as compliance standards. No order after EO 13891 other than EO 13992 names it in a held text. Later events on the acting order, tested under D6: EO 14148 sec. 2(g) and EO 14154 (both signed 2025-01-20, held official texts) revoke EO 13992 itself; neither contains reinstatement or revival wording for any order revoked by EO 13992 (searched for 'reinstat' in the held texts of EO 14148, 14154 and 14192; the only hits are in EO 14192 sec. 6(b)-(c), which reinstate OMB Circular A-4 (2003 version) and a Treasury-OMB memorandum of agreement), and EO 14192 sec. 3 sets a new regulatory cap for fiscal year 2025 under its own authority without naming this order. Revoking a revoking order is not a reinstatement, so the 2021-01-20 revocation of this order stands. The U.S. Code note confirms the ending: the machine current-law search found the OLRC note at 5 U.S.C. 601 note that EO 13891 'was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 13992, § 2, Jan. 20, 2021, 86 F.R. 7049'. The three dossier machine searches were read and copied. Own by-number scan (hyphenation and whitespace normalised) of the 6,652 held Federal Register text files in jobs/fr-originals for the bare number 13891 near 'order' or 'Executive Order': EO 13891 is named only in EO 13992 sec. 2 (other hits are Federal Register page numbers). Conflict, savings and the own-residual check are in conflict_resolutions and savings_residuals.

Reading record LSP-EO_13992: sec. 2 revokes EO 13891 whole with no effective-date wording (2021-01-20); sec. 3 directs OMB and agency heads to rescind 'any orders, rules, regulations, guidelines, or policies ... implementing or enforcing' the revoked orders 'as appropriate and consistent with applicable law, including the Administrative Procedure Act', and, where rescission cannot be finalized immediately, to provide exemptions; sec. 4(a) is a non-impairment clause; nothing is transferred and no exception names EO 13891. Own-residual check, reading EO 13891 in full (secs. 1-7): sec. 4(a) required each agency to 'finalize regulations, or amend existing regulations' setting out guidance-document processes within 300 days of OMB's memorandum, and sec. 6 had OMB issue memoranda and regulations. Regulations an agency finalized under sec. 4(a) are independent legal instruments that remain in force after the order is revoked until the agency rescinds them by notice and comment (the APA reference in EO 13992 sec. 3 says as much), so the order's implementing rules continue independently of it. The dossier's current-law leads (28 CFR part 813, 29 CFR part 1695, 45 CFR part 2509, 32 CFR part 339 and 49 CFR 5.39, which name EO 13891) are consistent with that reading but were not read as legal text (no held slice or sha256), so the state rests on the held texts of EO 13891 and EO 13992. The prefill was S4 (conflict): the conflict is resolved in conflict_resolutions and the savings state is continuing_independent, overruling the plain 'none' reading. Bounded search: EO 13891 and EO 13992 in full; the dossier's current-law leads and the three machine searches; the by-number scan.

EO 13892 (signed 2019-10-09, 84 FR 55239; read in full from the held Federal Register text, 45 clauses) states the policy of transparency and fairness in civil administrative enforcement and adjudication (sec. 1), defines terms (sec. 2), limits reliance on guidance documents (secs. 3-5), requires an opportunity to contest agency determinations (sec. 6), orders agency inspection rules (sec. 7), information-collection compliance (sec. 8), cooperative enforcement procedures (sec. 9), a SBREFA report (sec. 10) and general provisions and carve-outs (sec. 11). Own-terms: only report deadlines (sec. 9(b) 270 days, sec. 10 180 days) and conditions; no sunset or term. EO 13992 sec. 2 revokes it on signing, 2021-01-20 (LSP-EO_13992). Dossier missing line 'target provision not located: EO:13924': EO 13924 (2020-05-19, held official text, read in full) sec. 5(a) provides that pre-enforcement rulings under that subsection 'may be issued without regard to the requirements of section 6(a) of Executive Order 13892'; that is a partial change to the sec. 6(a) clause before the end and is attached as a later event (ACTOR_TEXT:EO:13924, effective on signing 2020-05-19) on the sec. 6 clause. The rest of EO 13924 only adopts EO 13892's definitions (sec. 2) and refers to pre-enforcement rulings under it; it does not revoke, suspend or extend EO 13892. No other order names EO 13892 except EO 13992 and EO 13924. Later events on the acting order, tested under D6: EO 14148 sec. 2(g) and EO 14154 (both signed 2025-01-20, held official texts) revoke EO 13992 itself; neither contains reinstatement or revival wording for any order revoked by EO 13992 (searched for 'reinstat' in the held texts of EO 14148, 14154 and 14192; the only hits are in EO 14192 sec. 6(b)-(c), which reinstate OMB Circular A-4 (2003 version) and a Treasury-OMB memorandum of agreement), and EO 14192 sec. 3 sets a new regulatory cap for fiscal year 2025 under its own authority without naming this order. Revoking a revoking order is not a reinstatement, so the 2021-01-20 revocation of this order stands. The U.S. Code note confirms the ending: the machine current-law search found the OLRC note at 5 U.S.C. 551 note that EO 13892 'was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 13992, § 2, Jan. 20, 2021, 86 F.R. 7049'. The dossier's three machine searches were read and copied. Own by-number scan (hyphenation and whitespace normalised) of the 6,652 held Federal Register text files in jobs/fr-originals for the bare number 13892 near 'order' or 'Executive Order': EO 13892 is named in EO 13924 and EO 13992 (other hits are page numbers in neighbouring documents). Savings and the own-residual check are in savings_residuals.

Reading record LSP-EO_13992: sec. 2 revokes EO 13892 whole with no effective-date wording (2021-01-20); sec. 3 directs OMB and agency heads to rescind implementing orders, rules, regulations, guidelines and policies (and to provide exemptions where rescission is not immediate); sec. 4(a) is a non-impairment clause; nothing is transferred and no exception names EO 13892. Own-residual check, reading EO 13892 in full (secs. 1-11): it created no entity, fund, property or right (sec. 11(c)). It did require each inspecting agency to publish a rule of agency procedure governing civil administrative inspections within 120 days (sec. 7) and to propose cooperative-enforcement procedures within 270 days (sec. 9). Any rule an agency published under those sections is an agency instrument that would outlive the order until rescinded under EO 13992 sec. 3, so a residual is possible in principle; the bounded search found none: the machine current-law searches name no CFR or U.S. Code provision that cites EO 13892 other than the OLRC note that records its revocation (5 U.S.C. 551 note), the OFR catalog shows only the revocation, and EO 13924 (the only held order besides EO 13992 that names it, see the later event) adds no continuing instrument. The prefill was S1 (transfer wording): the 'transfer' phrases belong to EO 13992 sec. 3 (rescission and abolition) and transfer no function; kept as none_after_bounded_search after reading both orders, with the sec. 7 rules recorded here as the limit of the search. Bounded search: EO 13892, EO 13992 and EO 13924 in full; current-law usc/ecfr searches; the by-number scan.

EO 13893 (signed 2019-10-10, 84 FR 55487; read in full from the held Federal Register text) institutionalises 'Administrative PAYGO': definitions (sec. 3), scope (sec. 4), agency proposal requirements with an offset (sec. 5), OMB instructions within 90 days and revocation of OMB Memorandum M-05-13 (sec. 6), waiver (sec. 7), additional deficit reduction (sec. 8) and general provisions (sec. 9). It has no sunset, term, condition tied to an end or report date; the dossier flags only the 'implemented consistent with applicable law' condition and lists no other-actor provision and no missing provision. EO 13992 sec. 2 revokes it on signing, 2021-01-20 (reading record LSP-EO_13992). Later events on the acting order, tested under D6: EO 14148 sec. 2(g) and EO 14154 (both signed 2025-01-20, held official texts) revoke EO 13992 itself; neither contains reinstatement or revival wording for any order revoked by EO 13992 (searched for 'reinstat' in the held texts of EO 14148, 14154 and 14192; the only hits are in EO 14192 sec. 6(b)-(c), which reinstate OMB Circular A-4 (2003 version) and a Treasury-OMB memorandum of agreement), and EO 14192 sec. 3 sets a new regulatory cap for fiscal year 2025 under its own authority without naming this order. Revoking a revoking order is not a reinstatement, so the 2021-01-20 revocation of this order stands. The U.S. Code note confirms the ending: the machine current-law search found the OLRC note at 5 U.S.C. 601 note that EO 13893 'was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 13992, § 2, Jan. 20, 2021, 86 F.R. 7049'. The dossier's three machine searches were read and copied. Own by-number scan (hyphenation and whitespace normalised) of the 6,652 held Federal Register text files in jobs/fr-originals for the bare number 13893 near 'order' or 'Executive Order': EO 13893 is named only in EO 13992 sec. 2 (other hits are Federal Register page numbers in neighbouring documents). Savings and the own-residual check are in savings_residuals.

Reading record LSP-EO_13992: sec. 2 revokes EO 13893 whole, no effective-date wording (2021-01-20); sec. 3 tells OMB and the agency heads to rescind implementing orders, rules, regulations, guidelines and policies and to abolish entities established under the revoked orders, 'as appropriate and consistent with applicable law'; sec. 4(a) is a general non-impairment clause for statutory authority and OMB budget functions; no function is transferred and no pending-matter or exception clause names EO 13893. Own-residual check, reading EO 13893 in full (secs. 1-9): it created no entity, fund, property or right (sec. 9(c) disclaims rights); its operative commands were agency submissions of administrative actions to OMB with offsets (sec. 5), OMB instructions (sec. 6), a waiver power (sec. 7) and a flexibility clause (sec. 8). Sec. 6 told the Director to revoke OMB Memorandum M-05-13; that revocation is a completed OMB act that EO 13992 does not revive, but it is an OMB act and not an effect of the order that outlives it. The only implementing document the order called for, OMB's instructions under sec. 6, is the kind of implementing guidance EO 13992 sec. 3 directs OMB to rescind. EO 13924 (signed May 19, 2020, 85 FR 31353-31356), read in full from the held official FR text, sets the policy of combating the economic consequences of COVID-19 by regulatory relief (sec. 1), defines terms by reference to EO 13892 (sec. 2), directs agency heads to use emergency authorities, to identify and rescind or waive regulatory standards, to speed pre-enforcement rulings and enforcement discretion, to apply fairness principles, to review their regulatory response and to report, and has OMB monitor (secs. 3-8), with general provisions (sec. 9). It has no term or sunset: it has no dated end, and the review and report in sec. 7 have no deadline except one OMB may set (sec. 8). EO 14018 sec. 1 (reading record LSP-EO_14018, read once in full) revokes the order with no effective-date wording, effective on signing 2021-02-24. The dossier's ACT record is built on the held official FR text of EO 14018 and carries the sec. 1 sentence naming the order; its scope is whole. The dossier's one missing line, 'target provision not located: EO:13892', was read: EO 13892 (2019-10-09, held official text) predates EO 13924 and cannot amend it, and EO 13924 only borrows EO 13892's definitions and its pre-enforcement ruling procedure (secs. 2 and 5), so the OFR edge is a cross-reference and is ruled out as a later event. The dossier's 32 clauses run contiguously from the first section to the signature line, so the inventory is kept as is. D6 (any later event that ended or changed a clause): a by-number scan of all 6,652 held official FR order texts finds EO 13924 named only in EO 14018; the OFR catalog edges (5 rows) are 4 rows for the EO 14018 revocation and one cross-reference to EO 13892; the USC note at 5 U.S.C. 601 note records only the EO 14018 revocation. Savings: none_after_bounded_search, see savings_residuals.

Reading record LSP-EO_14018 (EO 14018, 86 FR 11855-11856, read once in full): sec. 1 revokes five Executive orders and two memoranda with no effective-date wording; sec. 2 treats rules and policies implementing a listed order as separate acts for the agencies to consider rescinding and abolishes entities created under the listed actions as appropriate and consistent with law; sec. 3(a) is a no-impair clause for statutory agency authority and OMB functions only; there is no successor delegation, transfer of functions or funds, pending-matter clause or exception. The two transfer-wording hits the machine counted are words in the title of a revoked Memorandum ('Delegation of Certain Authority Under the Federal Service Labor-Management Relations Statute'), not an operative transfer. Pre-enforcement rulings, waivers and rescissions issued under it are acts of the agencies under their own authority and EO 13892, not provisions of EO 13924, which EO 14018 sec. 2 treats as separate acts to consider rescinding; sec. 9(d) disclaims private rights. EO 13927 (signed 2020-06-04, 85 FR 35165-35170), read in full from the held FR text, directs agencies to speed infrastructure and recovery actions during the COVID-19 national emergency: transportation, Army civil works and Federal-lands projects (secs. 3-5), NEPA, ESA and Clean Water Act emergency procedures (secs. 6-8), other emergency authorities (sec. 9) and general provisions (sec. 10). Most operative sections set a 30-day report and then status reports 'at least every 30 days for the duration of the national emergency'. The machine own-term kinds (condition, emergency_duration, fixed_term, report_deadline) are not ends: 30-day periods are deadlines, and the emergency-duration wording would end the recurring reports only when the emergency ended, which was after 2021-01-20 (no held source records an earlier end). The order has no sunset or termination clause. No clause's first end needs a report date, so the order is not blocked on the report-deadline question. EO 13990 (86 FR 7037-7043, read in full; reading record scale/readings/LSP-EO_13990.json) sec. 7(a) revokes it, effective on signing, 2021-01-20; the U.S. Code note to 5 U.S.C. 601 says the same (86 FR 7041). The dossier lists no missing provision; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR-original texts finds EO 13927 named only in EO 13990. EO 14148 and EO 14154 (2025) revoke EO 13990 but name none of the six orders and reinstate nothing. Inventory correction: the dossier splits the tail of sec. 8(c) into a separate fragment clause 'sec8-a' ('(a)(i). Such status reports shall thereafter be provided...'); inventory_overrides merge it into sec8-c. All other spans are copied unchanged, so 44 clauses cover the operative text from sec. 1 through sec. 10(c) with no gap or overlap.

rationales.exact_text: Reading record scale/readings/LSP-EO_13990.json (EO 13990, 86 FR 7037-7043, read once in full): sec. 7(a) revokes EO 13927 with no savings, pending-matter or transition clause; sec. 8(a) saves only statutory agency authority; sec. 7(f) tells the OMB Director and agency heads to rescind issuances implementing or enforcing the revoked orders; nothing is transferred. Own-residual check, reading EO 13927 in full: it directs agencies to expedite projects and to report once and then every 30 days for the duration of the national emergency; it creates no right, benefit, property or fund (sec. 10(c) disclaims rights) and no body. The recurring reports were continuing duties of the order, and the revocation ended them; nothing in EO 13990 keeps them running. Emergency actions agencies took under their own statutory authorities are independent of the order. S0 prefill (none_after_bounded_search) KEPT. Bounded search: EO 13927 and EO 13990 in full; a by-number scan of all held FR-original texts; the U.S. Code note to 5 U.S.C. 601 (repeats the revocation).

EO 13989 (signed 2021-01-20, 86 FR 7029-7035), read in full from the held official FR text, sets the Ethics Pledge (sec. 1), definitions (sec. 2), waivers (sec. 3), administration (sec. 4), enforcement (sec. 5) and general provisions (sec. 6). The order has no term, sunset or termination clause; the dossier's fixed_term and condition terms are the pledge periods, the sec. 5(b) sanction duration and the 'consistent with applicable law' clause, none of which ends a clause of the order before the revocation. EO 14148 sec. 2(e) revokes the whole order with no effective-date wording, so effective on signing 2025-01-20. The dossier's missing line 'target provision not located: EO:14091' was read: EO 14091 sec. 2 (Agency Equity Teams) uses 'appointees, as defined in Executive Order 13989', a borrowed definition; it amends, extends or ends nothing in EO 13989, so it is ruled out as a later event, and EO 14091 was itself revoked by EO 14148 sec. 2(bbb). The dossier's 64-clause inventory is contiguous from sec. 1 through sec. 6(d) and was kept, except that the one-line list intro sec. 2(c) ('Gift':) was merged by override with its first item because the claim-checker cannot verify a quotation of fewer than 6 words and 30 characters (63 clauses); the pledge paragraphs sit inside clauses sec1 and sec1-c and are discussed there. The Code note at 5 U.S.C. 7301 note (MENTIONS.csv role eo_note_ended_status) states EO 13989 'was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 14148, sec. 2(e), Jan. 20, 2025, 90 F.R. 8237', consistent with this ending (a machine-extracted lead, not relied on).

Reading record LSP-EO_14148 (official FR text 90 FR 8237, read once in full, text_sha256 65bf2d86... verified on disk): sec. 2 revokes 78 listed executive actions with no effective-date, delayed-effect or phase-in wording, so each revocation took effect on signing, 2025-01-20; sec. 3(b) directs the DPC and NEC Directors to review and rescind, replace or amend agency actions taken under the listed orders (it preserves no provision, office or right of any listed order); sec. 4(a) is a no-impair clause for statutory authority and OMB functions only; there is no successor delegation, no transfer of functions, funds or property, no pending-matter clause and no exception for any listed order. Own-residual check, reading EO 13989 in full (secs. 1-6): sec. 1 makes every appointee appointed on or after 2021-01-20 'contractually committed' to the pledge, pledge para. 9 incorporates the Order into the agreement as binding, and sec. 5(a) makes the commitments enforceable by the United States by debarment or civil proceedings. Pledges signed before 2025-01-20 are completed individual undertakings, some with periods that run 1 to 2 years or more after the signer's appointment or departure (paras. 2-6) plus a possible bar of up to 5 years under sec. 5(b). EO 14148 sec. 2(e) revokes the order without cancelling signed pledges, sec. 3 waivers or the pledge files kept under sec. 4(e), and revocation of an order does not by itself discharge obligations already assumed under it, so these accrued undertakings survive the order (accrued). How or whether they are enforced after the revocation is not decided by any held source, and the claim does not assert it. No function, fund or property was transferred or re-delegated by EO 13989 or EO 14148; the OGE, OMB and agency duties in sec. 4 rest on the order and end with it. Prefill was 'review' (S1_transfer_wording): decided from the reading and the order as transferred_or_accrued. Bounded search: every held official FR text (EO 1 through EO 14435) was searched for the number 13989 and the title; only EO 14148 sec. 2(e) names it as a target, EO 14091 (revoked by EO 14148 sec. 2(bbb)) borrows its definition of 'appointees', and EO 13983 (2021) concerns EO 13770; OFR edges show only those; the three machine searches were read.

EO 14018 (signed 2021-02-24, 86 FR 11855-11856), read in full from the held official FR text: sec. 1 revokes seven Presidential actions; sec. 2 implementation (agencies consider rescinding implementing actions; entities established under the revoked actions abolished as appropriate); sec. 3 general provisions. No term or sunset. EO 14148 sec. 2(z) (reading record LSP-EO_14148) revokes it in full effective on signing 2025-01-20, no effective-date wording, no exception. The dossier inventory (one truncated clause) is replaced by seven clauses covering secs. 1-3(c); the override offsets were cut from the held text file and the gap check shows only the signature block outside them. OFR notes name only EO 14148 as acting on EO 14018; no held official text other than EO 14148 names EO 14018. Savings: completed revocations accrued (transferred_or_accrued).

Reading record LSP-EO_14148 (reused from Lambertini II after re-verifying text_sha256 65bf2d86...): sec. 2 revokes 78 listed actions with no effective-date wording, so each revocation took effect on signing 2025-01-20; sec. 3 directs agencies to end implementation, tells the DPC and NEC Directors to review and rescind actions taken under the listed orders, and the NSA to review NSMs; sec. 4(a) is a no-impair clause for statutory authority and OMB functions only; there is no successor delegation, transfer of functions, funds or property, pending-matter clause or exception for any listed order, and no revival wording. Own-residual check, reading EO 14018 in full (secs. 1-3): sec. 1 revoked EO 13772, EO 13828, EO 13924, EO 13967, EO 13979 and the memoranda of January 29, 2020 and September 2, 2020; sec. 2 directed agencies to consider rescinding implementing actions and provided that personnel positions, committees, task forces or other entities established under the revoked actions 'shall be abolished, as appropriate'. These are executed acts: the revoked orders and memoranda stayed revoked from 2021-02-24 and the entities abolished under sec. 2 stayed abolished. EO 14148 revokes EO 14018 but contains no wording reviving any of the seven actions it revoked (the general non-revival rule governs; EO 14148 sec. 3(b) only directs a review of actions taken under listed orders), so the completed revocations and abolitions accrued and remain after the revocation. No function, fund or property was transferred. Prefill 'review' (S1 transfer wording): overruled to transferred_or_accrued on these completed acts. Bounded search: every held official FR text was grepped for 14018 (only EO 14148 names it), OFR catalog edges, the OLRC notes at 5 U.S.C. 551 note, 601 note, 7103 note, 12 U.S.C. 5301 note and 40 U.S.C. 3101 note (all print the revoked orders as revoked by EO 14018) and the three machine searches were read.
