EO 14020 (signed 2021-03-08, 86 FR 13797-13801), read in full from the held official FR text, states the gender-equity policy (sec. 1), establishes the White House Gender Policy Council and its functions, co-chairs and 37-seat membership (sec. 2), requires a government-wide Strategy within 200 days (sec. 3), implementation, reporting and the National Action Plan (sec. 4), terminates the NSPM-16 Working Group (sec. 5), defines terms (sec. 6) and has general provisions (sec. 7). It has no sunset or termination clause for the Council; the dossier's 'sunset_date' lead is the sec. 5 termination of another body and its 'condition' lead is the 'consistent with applicable law' clause, neither an end of this order. EO 14148 sec. 2(bb) revokes the whole order with no effective-date wording, so effective on signing 2025-01-20. The dossier's other actor provision ACT:EO:14020>EO:14168 (sec. 7(b), held FR text 90 FR 8615) rescinds EO 14020 and dissolves the Council on the same day, effective on signing with no delayed wording; it is attached to every clause as a concurrent second end. The dossier inventory stopped inside sec. 3(c) (the segmenter treated the cited 'Executive Order 13985 ...' as a new document, leaving 6,267 characters including all of secs. 4-7 unlisted), so the inventory was corrected by override: the dossier clauses through sec. 3(b) are kept at their spans except three merges of very short clauses (sec. 2(b)(vi)+(vii) and Council seats (g)(i)+(ii) and (g)(iv)+(v), whose quotations the claim-checker cannot verify at under 6 words and 30 characters), and sec. 3(c) and secs. 4-7 are supplied as 16 corrected clauses (75 clauses in all). Dossier missing lines for EO 12250, 13995, 14091, 14121 and 14126 were each read: EO 12250 is cited by EO 14020 sec. 4(a) and predates it; EO 13995 is cited by sec. 3(b); EO 14091, 14121 and 14126 recite or borrow definitions from EO 14020 and amend, extend or end nothing in it. They are ruled out as later events. The Code note at 42 U.S.C. 2000e note (role eo_note_ended_status) states EO 14020 'was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 14148, sec. 2(bb), Jan. 20, 2025, 90 F.R. 8238, and Ex. Ord. No. 14168, sec. 7(b), Jan. 20, 2025, 90 F.R. 8617', consistent with this ending and the concurrent second end (a machine-extracted lead, not relied on).

EO 14089 (signed 2022-12-13, 87 FR 77459-77461), read in full from the held official FR text, states the policy (sec. 1), directs the Secretary of State to establish the President's Advisory Council on African Diaspora Engagement within 180 days (sec. 2), fixes membership, 2-year member terms, a Chair and Executive Director (sec. 3), functions (sec. 4), administration with quarterly meetings (sec. 5) and general provisions including FACA (sec. 6). It has no termination or sunset clause. EO 14148 sec. 2(aaa) (reading record LSP-EO_14148) revokes it with no effective-date wording, effective on signing 2025-01-20. Dossier missing lines read: (1) EO 14109 (88 FR 68447, read in full; effective 2023-09-29 under its sec. 6) sec. 1(cc) continues the Council until 2025-09-30; it is attached as a later event to the Council clauses (secs. 2 through 6(a)); it extends the committee's FACA life, amends no text, and the continuance date falls after the 2025-01-20 revocation, so it does not move the first end. (2) EO 13985 (held official text) does not name EO 14089; EO 14089 sec. 4(b)(i) only refers to the efforts coordinated under EO 13985, and EO 13985 was revoked by EO 14148 sec. 2(a) on the same day, so it changes nothing earlier and is ruled out. The 2-year member terms are not an end of the clauses. The inventory is the dossier's 22 contiguous clauses from sec. 1 to the signature line and is kept. No other held official text names EO 14089. Savings: none found.

Reading record LSP-EO_14148: sec. 2 revokes 78 listed actions, no effective-date wording, so effective on signing 2025-01-20; sec. 3 directs agencies to end implementation and tells the DPC and NEC Directors to review and rescind actions taken under the listed orders; sec. 4(a) is a no-impair clause for statutory authority and OMB functions only; there is no successor delegation, transfer of functions or funds, pending-matter clause or exception for any listed order. Own-residual check, reading EO 14089 in full (secs. 1-6): it revokes or amends no order, transfers no function, fund or property and creates no right (sec. 6(d)). It created an advisory council in the Department of State whose appointments are made by the Secretary of State for 2-year terms without compensation; the Council, its terms and its advice function ended with the order. The one residual lead is EO 14109 sec. 1(cc), which continued the Council as a FACA committee until 2025-09-30 and was not itself revoked by EO 14148; that continuance only extends a committee that Executive Order 14089 established and supplies no separate mandate, appointment power or duty, and EO 14148 is the later and specific act ending the order, so no continuing effect is found. EO 14115 (signed 2024-02-01, 89 FR 7605-7608), read in full from the held official FR text, finds a threat to the peace, security and stability of the West Bank and declares a national emergency, blocks the property of persons determined under sec. 1 (secs. 1-3), suspends their entry (sec. 4), prohibits evasion and conspiracy (sec. 5), makes IEEPA determinations on donations and notice (secs. 6 and 8), defines terms (sec. 7), authorizes Treasury rules and redelegation (sec. 9), excepts official business (sec. 10), provides for reports to the Congress (sec. 11) and has general provisions (sec. 12). The order has no term, sunset or termination clause: its only dossier own-term leads are the 'consistent with applicable law' condition and the sec. 4(d) comparison to Proclamation 8693, neither an end. EO 14148 sec. 2(hhh) revokes the whole order with no effective-date wording, so effective on signing 2025-01-20. The dossier has no missing line, conflict or current-law lead for this order. The dossier inventory (43 clauses) began after the findings paragraph and split sec. 1(b)(ii) in the middle of a sentence, so the inventory was corrected by override: the preamble findings are added as one clause, and the two fragments of sec. 1(b)(ii) are merged, and the two short items of sec. 1(a)(i)(B), (3) and (4), are merged (too short for the claim-checker to verify) (42 clauses in all). The national-emergency question is stated in the lead clause and in savings_residuals. No amendment, extension, partial revocation or supersession of EO 14115 appears in any held text or OFR edge before 2025-01-20. The Code note at 50 U.S.C. 1701 note ('West Bank') states 'Ex. Ord. No. 14115, Feb. 1, 2024, 89 F.R. 7605, revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 14148, sec. 2(hhh), Jan. 20, 2025, 90 F.R. 8240', consistent with this ending (a machine-extracted lead, not relied on).

Reading record LSP-EO_14148 (official FR text 90 FR 8237, read once in full, text_sha256 65bf2d86... verified on disk): sec. 2 revokes 78 listed executive actions with no effective-date, delayed-effect or phase-in wording, so each revocation took effect on signing, 2025-01-20; sec. 3(b) directs the DPC and NEC Directors to review and rescind, replace or amend agency actions taken under the listed orders (it preserves no provision, office or right of any listed order); sec. 4(a) is a no-impair clause for statutory authority and OMB functions only; there is no successor delegation, no transfer of functions, funds or property, no pending-matter clause and no exception for any listed order. Own-residual check, reading EO 14115 in full (preamble and secs. 1-12): the order declared a national emergency under IEEPA and the NEA, blocked all property and interests in property of persons determined under sec. 1 and suspended their entry (sec. 4), and sec. 9 authorized the Treasury Secretary to issue rules and to redelegate functions within Treasury. Effects of the order that attached before 2025-01-20 are not undone by its revocation: property blocked and transactions prohibited or evaded under secs. 1-5 before that date, and any liability for violations before it, are accrued matters of an IEEPA instrument, and EO 14148 sec. 2(hhh) revokes the order with no savings clause and no statement of what happens to them (accrued). The sec. 9 redelegation authority and any Treasury listings made under it are exercises of functions the order conferred; they end with the order and no redelegation or regulation under it appears in the eCFR machine search. The national emergency declared in the preamble is not terminated by EO 14148 in so many words; if it was not continued by a notice published within 90 days before 2025-02-01 it lapsed under 50 U.S.C. 1622(d) after the first end, and I found no such notice in any held source, so the claim relies on the revocation of the order as the first end and asserts nothing about the emergency after it. Prefill was 'review' (S1_transfer_wording): decided from the reading and the order as transferred_or_accrued. Bounded search: every held official FR text (EO 1 through EO 14435) was searched for the number 14115 and the title; only EO 14148 sec. 2(hhh) names it as a target (the EO 9372 and 9386 hits are page-index numbers); OFR edges list only EO 14148 and the Proclamation 8693 cross-reference; the three machine searches were read.

EO 7921 (June 30, 1938) extended the existence of the Quetico-Superior Committee for four years, from June 30, 1938 to June 30, 1942. The Quetico-Superior Committee was created by EO 6783 (1934) for a limited period and kept alive by successive four-year extension orders (EOs 7921, 9213, 9741, 10134, 10541, 10767, 11031) and amended by EOs 9890, 10589 and 11031. EO 11342 of April 10, 1967 (32 FR 5827) established a committee of the same name anew (sec. 1), let it carry forward the old committee's uncompleted business (sec. 5) and in sec. 6 superseded EO 6783 and all nine continuing or amending orders; it states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. That supersession was a formal cleanup: each extension order had already run out on the fixed date it states, and the last extension (EO 11031 sec. 1) ended on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification disposition row for EO 6783 lists no continuation after EO 11031, the OFR catalog has no Quetico order between EO 11031 and EO 11342, and EO 11342 establishes the committee anew, so the committee lapsed on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification ('Superseded by EO 11342') and the OFR catalog note were used only as leads; the dates come from the order texts. Texts were checked against the text layer of the saved official Federal Register scans (fr-originals); no page-image comparison was made. This order's only operative provision is the extension itself, so its operation ended on 1942-06-30; the 1967 supersession is recorded as a later event.

Neither this order nor EO 11342 contains a savings clause preserving any provision of this order. EO 11342 sec. 5 lets the new committee carry forward uncompleted business and succeed to records and property of the committee provided for in EO 6783; that is a successor-order transition for the committee's affairs, not a continuation of this order's terms.

Its whole operative content is an amendment of Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873, as amended (the 1989 OFR disposition table: 'Amended EO 9'; 'Revoked by EO 11408'). EO 11408 of April 25, 1968 (33 FR 6459, saved official text read in full) revoked EO 9 itself in section 1 and in section 2 revoked 'All prior Executive orders insofar as they interpret or amend Executive Order No. 9'; EO 11408 section 2 names it expressly in its list of revoked amendatory orders. The order has no expiry, condition or temporary term, the OFR catalog and the saved-text corpus show no earlier amendment or revocation, and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches show no current citation. However, the order names the Social Security Board, which was abolished in 1946, so an earlier cessation is possible and the first end is not asserted (see gap); EO 11408's revocation is recorded as a later event. EO 11408 contains no savings, transition or continuation clause. Its section 1 revoked Executive Order No. 9 of January 17, 1873 (the dual federal-state office-holding prohibition) itself, and section 2 revoked every prior order insofar as it interpreted or amended that order. This order's only operative content is an amendment of (an exception to) that 1873 order, so once the prohibition itself was revoked nothing remained for the exception to operate on, and no office, fund, property, entitlement or enforceable right was created by the order that could survive; office-holding done under the permission before 1968 was lawful when done and is a completed historical fact, not a continuing effect.

EO 8546 (Sept. 24, 1940; 5 FR 3817-3818) creates the Defense Communications Board (para. 1), gives it planning functions for national emergencies (para. 2), sets its chairmanship and secretary (para. 3), its scope and broadcasting studies (para. 4), committees (paras. 5-6), consultation (para. 7), the advisory role of the Interdepartment Radio Advisory Committee during war or national emergency (para. 8) and reporting to the President (para. 9). Later events: EO 8960 (Dec. 6, 1941) substituted the Treasury officer named in paras. 1 and 3; EO 9183 (June 15, 1942) renamed the Board the Board of War Communications and amended this order accordingly; neither ended a clause (word substitutions; the clauses continue as amended). EO 8964 and EO 9089 gave the Board further powers without amending this order. The orders rest on wartime and emergency powers (Communications Act sec. 606 and the national emergency); neither the orders nor sec. 606 had lapsed before Feb. 24, 1947: the state of war declared in December 1941 had not been terminated, and no concurrent resolution ending the sec. 606 powers is recorded in the bounded sources; no earlier presidential order ending any of these provisions appears in the OFR catalog or the saved order texts. EO 9831 (Feb. 24, 1947; 12 FR 1363) para. 1 abolishes the Board, created 'as the Defense Communications Board by Executive Order No. 8546', and para. 2 revokes EO 8546; it states no effective date, so it took effect on issuance. Every clause therefore first ended on 1947-02-24, the whole-order end. The two current-law hits (47 U.S.C. 606 note) print EO 9831 itself, which confirms the abolition and revocation; no current predicate. The 1989 Codification row: 'Amended by EOs 8960, 9183 ... Revoked by EO 9831'.

EO 9831 para. 1 abolishes the Board of War Communications and transfers all its property and records to the Federal Communications Commission; para. 2 revokes the five orders without any savings clause. EO 8744 (April 24, 1941; 6 FR 2118-2119, held official FR scan text, closing tag '[No. 8744]') has a single operative paragraph: an incumbent of a position covered into the classified service by section 1 of EO 8743 who is involuntarily separated by reduction in force, abolition of the position or liquidation of the agency between the date of EO 8743 and the effective date of its section 1 may acquire a classified status for transfer, provided (among other things) that 'he obtains such transfer within one year from the date of his separation'. By its own terms the authorization could therefore operate only for separations up to the effective date of section 1 of EO 8743 (January 1, 1942 under EO 8743 Sec. 2, earlier for positions that fell vacant after June 30, 1941) and transfers within one year after them. The EO 12608 revocation of September 9, 1987 is a formal cleanup that follows this earlier cessation and is recorded as a later event, not the first end. The exact last day cannot yet be fixed: EO 8743 Sec. 2 was itself amended (EOs 9230, 9358, 9678, 9712 and others touch EO 8743) and it is not established whether any amendment moved the effective date of its section 1; and a transfer deadline is a condition of eligibility, so the date must be fixed from the text, not inferred.

EO 12608 Sec. 1 provides that notwithstanding the revocation of EO 8744, benefits already conferred under it before revocation shall not be affected: classified status acquired under the order stands.

This order's only operative provision is the extension itself, so its operation ended on 1946-06-30; the 1967 supersession is recorded as a later event.

EO 9635 (September 29, 1945) reorganized the Navy Department in ten numbered paragraphs, read in the held govinfo scan of 10 FR 12419 and its continuation on 12421. It has no expiry or condition of its own. Its main statutory basis, Title I of the First War Powers Act, was by its sec. 401 in force during the war and for six months after its termination; the war had not been terminated by April 1950, and EO 10123 treats the order as still in force, so no earlier statutory lapse is shown. The one earlier event is EO 9904 (November 13, 1947), which replaced the text of para. 8 (order of succession), so the original para. 8 ended on that date. EO 10123 (15 FR 2265) then revoked EO 9635 and EO 9904 without a stated effective date, so every other paragraph ended on its signing date, April 20, 1950, which is the whole-order end. The National Security Act of 1947 and its 1949 amendments, which reorganized the military establishment, were not read here; no held source (OFR catalog, U.S. Code notes, 1989 Codification table) records that they revoked or replaced any paragraph, which is a limit of this bounded search rather than a finding. Savings: EO 10123 keeps EOs 8984 and 9096 revoked (non-revival), an effect now resting on EO 10123. The OFR catalog and the 1989 Codification table (a lead) list no other amendment.

EO 10123 has no savings clause for the Navy organization of EO 9635, which thereafter rested on the statutes (para. 9 itself disclaims any change to the Secretary's statutory authority). Its one qualification is that the revocation 'shall not be construed as reviving' EOs 8984 and 9096, which para. 10 of EO 9635 had revoked. That completed revocation therefore continues, but its continuing basis is EO 10123's non-revival sentence, an independent later source, not EO 9635. No other surviving right, office or obligation of EO 9635 was found.

EO 9741 (June 25, 1946) extended the committee for four years from June 30, 1946 to June 30, 1950. The Quetico-Superior Committee was created by EO 6783 (1934) for a limited period and kept alive by successive four-year extension orders (EOs 7921, 9213, 9741, 10134, 10541, 10767, 11031) and amended by EOs 9890, 10589 and 11031. EO 11342 of April 10, 1967 (32 FR 5827) established a committee of the same name anew (sec. 1), let it carry forward the old committee's uncompleted business (sec. 5) and in sec. 6 superseded EO 6783 and all nine continuing or amending orders; it states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. That supersession was a formal cleanup: each extension order had already run out on the fixed date it states, and the last extension (EO 11031 sec. 1) ended on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification disposition row for EO 6783 lists no continuation after EO 11031, the OFR catalog has no Quetico order between EO 11031 and EO 11342, and EO 11342 establishes the committee anew, so the committee lapsed on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification ('Superseded by EO 11342') and the OFR catalog note were used only as leads; the dates come from the order texts. Texts were checked against the text layer of the saved official Federal Register scans (fr-originals); no page-image comparison was made. This order's only operative provision is the extension itself, so its operation ended on 1950-06-30; the 1967 supersession is recorded as a later event.

Neither this order nor EO 11342 contains a savings clause preserving any provision of this order. EO 11342 sec. 5 lets the new committee carry forward uncompleted business and succeed to records and property of the committee provided for in EO 6783; that is a successor-order transition for the committee's affairs, not a continuation of this order's terms.

Murie (printed 'Glaus' in the text layer) to a vacancy, and amended EO 6783 accordingly. The Quetico-Superior Committee was created by EO 6783 (1934) for a limited period and kept alive by successive four-year extension orders (EOs 7921, 9213, 9741, 10134, 10541, 10767, 11031) and amended by EOs 9890, 10589 and 11031. EO 11342 of April 10, 1967 (32 FR 5827) established a committee of the same name anew (sec. 1), let it carry forward the old committee's uncompleted business (sec. 5) and in sec. 6 superseded EO 6783 and all nine continuing or amending orders; it states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. That supersession was a formal cleanup: each extension order had already run out on the fixed date it states, and the last extension (EO 11031 sec. 1) ended on June 30, 1966. The 1989 Codification disposition row for EO 6783 lists no continuation after EO 11031, the OFR catalog has no Quetico order between EO 11031 and EO 11342, and EO 11342 establishes the committee anew, so the committee lapsed on June 30, 1966. Texts were checked against the text layer of the saved official Federal Register scans (fr-originals); no page-image comparison was made. The authority to consult and the amendment of EO 6783 had no term of their own and operated only while the committee existed, so they ceased with the committee on June 30, 1966. The appointment was a one-time act completed on issuance (if it were instead dated by the appointee's tenure, that tenure could not outlast the committee, so the whole-order end is unchanged). Whole-order end: 1966-06-30.

Neither this order nor EO 11342 contains a savings clause preserving any provision of this order. EO 11342 sec. 5 lets the new committee carry forward uncompleted business and succeed to records and property of the committee provided for in EO 6783; that is a successor-order transition for the committee's affairs, not a continuation of this order's terms.

The military department discretion is part of the single construction authority. Immediate commencement and transmission/publication implement that invocation and do not create separate continuing construction authority after emergency termination. No performance or congressional transmission date is asserted. The original makes the 10 USC2808 invocation available immediately under the EO12722 Iraq emergency. EO12722 and EO12724 precede EO12734, so missing machine target provisions for those actors cannot establish a later cessation of this order. EO12771 expressly leaves the Iraq emergency unaffected. EO13303 addresses selected property, and EO12817 transfer authority, rather than construction authority. No earlier cessation is identified in the held chain or selected bounded later-order search.

Complete operative source spans selected by independent comparison with the held original. The original has one operative construction invocation plus effective/publication implementation. It invokes 10 USC2808 according to its terms, for Defense and military department Secretaries, and contains no finite project, report, fixed expiration, or separate independent program. EO13350 explicitly revokes EO12734 and terminates its underlying emergency; section 10 makes that action effective July 30, 2004 at 12:01 a.m. EDT, not July 29 signing.

Treasury action, compelled bank transfers, Federal Reserve receiving/holding/investing/transferring, implementation, definitions, noncreation of enforceable rights and immediate/publication instructions were each considered. None supplies prospective independent transfer authority after express revocation. Section 4 protects qualifying historical conduct; its accrued effects are separately preserved. No actual administrative completion or congressional transmission event is inferred. Sections 1-3 establish continuing Treasury, bank-transfer and Federal Reserve authority with conditional transfers; an actual transfer does not exhaust the authority to address other assets or repayments. Neither an assumed transfer date nor UNSCR778 adoption is used as an end. The held chain identifies EO13350 as the express revocation, effective under its section 10 on July 30, 2004 at 12:01 a.m. EDT.

EO 13792 (Review of Designations Under the Antiquities Act, signed 2017-04-26, 82 FR 20429-20431) was read in full from the held official Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13792.txt, OCR text layer of three PDF pages; page images were not inspected and requires_page_check is false). Operative content: Sec. 1 policy; Sec. 2(a)-(c) Secretary of the Interior review of monument designations, factors and consultation; Sec. 2(d)-(e) interim report in 45 days and final report in 120 days (report deadlines, never ends); Sec. 3 general provisions. It has no sunset and no own-terms ending. The first and only end found is Sec. 7(a) of EO 13990 (signed 2021-01-20, 86 FR 7037; held official text, Sec. 7 and Sec. 8 read in full): 'Executive Order 13792 of April 26, 2017 (Review of Designations Under the Antiquities Act) ... are hereby revoked.' The revocation of EO 13792 is unconditional (the exception wording in Sec. 7 concerns only EO 13834, EO 13920 and memoranda) and EO 13990 states no delayed effective date, so it took effect on signing, 2021-01-20. The three machine searches (U.S. Code release 119-121 and eCFR as of 2026-10-14: 0 hits; OFR catalog: 2 hits, both EO 13990, no reinstatement candidate) were read and carry no coverage warning; they show no earlier ending and no later revival. Judgment on performance: the Secretary's review and reports ordered by Sec. 2 may have been completed in 2017, but no held source dates them, a report deadline is not an end and the order is not self-terminating, so the order is treated as operative until revoked on 2021-01-20. The independent reviewer should test that judgment.

EO 10192 (December 15, 1950, 15 FR 9029) was read in the held official Federal Register extract (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10192.txt, 19,424 chars). The order is only the two numbered amendments at about chars 15,127-15,308; the rest of the extract is neighbouring Federal Register material including EO 10193. It amends EO 10129 of June 3, 1950 (President's Commission on Migratory Labor, held): para 1 changes the paragraph 3 report date from 'December 15, 1950' to 'March 1, 1951'; para 2 changes 'Thirty days' to 'Sixty days' in paragraph 8 (EO 10129 para 8 as issued: 'Thirty days after rendition of its report to the President, the Commission shall cease to exist unless otherwise determined by further Executive Order'). The first end is EO 10236 (signed 1951-04-26, 16 FR 3607; held official text): 'paragraph 8 ... as amended by paragraph 2 of Executive Order No. 10192 ... be, and it is hereby, further amended to read as follows: "8. The Commission shall cease to exist at the end of May 31, 1951."' Clause 2 (the 'Sixty days' wording) was replaced on 1951-04-26; clause 1 (the changed report date) was spent when the Commission ceased to exist at the end of 1951-05-31, which is also the whole-order end. A report deadline is not an end and the actual report date is not held, so I treated the amendment of a deadline as ending with the body whose report it governed; the independent reviewer should test that choice. The machine searches (usc 0 hits, ecfr 0 hits, OFR catalog 1 hit) carry no coverage warning; the single catalog hit points at EO 10263 only because of a mis-attributed date and is resolved above.

EO 10999 (Assigning Emergency Preparedness Functions to the Secretary of Commerce, signed 1962-02-16, 27 FR 1527-1532) was read in full from the held official Federal Register extract (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10999.txt, 24,413 chars; page images not inspected). The extract begins with the tail of EO 10998 (Agriculture, Secs. 8-12) and ends with the opening of EO 11000 (Labor); neither is part of EO 10999. The machine draft inventory had 46 records with duplicated sub-items that mixed those neighbours, so I replaced it with the 13 sections of EO 10999 (Secs. 1-13) using absolute character spans in the held file. EO 10999 has no sunset. Its first end is EO 11490 (signed 1969-10-28, 34 FR 17567): Sec. 3015 'The following are hereby revoked:' lists '(7) Executive Order No. 10999 of February 16, 1962' (official Federal Register text jobs/family-rule-tail/output/texts/EO_11490_tail.txt, and the APP transcription); the OLRC note at 42 U.S.C. 5195 note independently records that EO 10999 'was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 11490, Oct. 28, 1969, 34 F.R. 17567'. EO 11490 states no effective date or delay, so it took effect on signing, 1969-10-28. Sec. 3014 (retention of existing authority) is expressly 'except as provided by Section 3015' and so does not save EO 10999. Search scope: current-law:usc (one editorial note stating the revocation), current-law:ecfr (no section in the eCFR search hits lists EO 10999), later-events:ofr_catalog (all hits are EO 11490); none has a coverage warning. The dossier's missing item (EO 10952, a Department of Defense order named in Sec. 6) is only a cross-reference and is not an acting instrument for EO 10999.
